# Backlog

Living document — items deferred from earlier sessions plus future ideas with
the reasoning for the deferral. Update when items ship or new ideas land.

## Active themes

### Data foundation (current focus)
Building out player, team, and environmental data coverage so future modeling
work has rich features to draw from. Examples in progress or queued below.

### Daily ops + iteration
Predict → evaluate → improve → export, with incremental fixes as exports surface
issues. Park factors and reliever-as-starter fix shipped recently in this mode.

---

## Feature backlog

Roughly ordered by expected value vs effort. Items marked **[DEFERRED]** have a
specific reason they're not being built now.

### MLB / baseball

  - **Built:** the spec records both rulings, and the coverage receipt prints each season's `coverage gate` line (the finished regular-season and postseason games with lines for both teams, MEETS or BELOW 98%). That line is the one 2(a) reads for 2022.
- **Codex round 2 on #710 (the one fix round, addendum 170 item 3):**
  - **The carried level (P1, spec section 4):** the first form was a normalized weighted mean with a 0.75 factor on the previous season's weights, and that factor cancels. At a season opener C stayed at last season's level while v1's rating had regressed 25% toward 1500, so Δ over-subtracted. C is now a walk built as v1 builds the rating: it starts at 0 (the league level), moves `C ← (1 − ρ)·C + ρ·S` after each game, and is shrunk `C ← 0.75·C` at a new season. **For the architect:** this is a correction to Code's proposal, inside the "noted, not yet ruled" set for 11-02.   - **A tie for the most attempts (P2):** names no quarterback; the receipt counts such team-games. The spec's identity rule then reads the game before.
  - **A closing block that is not an object (P2, #627 receipt):** the file is unreadable and listed, and the later closings are still read.

**2026-10-27 — BUILT (ARCHITECT 2026-10-27, addendum 169 item 4; 08:30 ET): Step B's host timer, the laptop's standing routine, the Today tab's coverage source; the cups' daily schedule read (#707). No bar moves.**
- **Item 4, verbatim:**
  - "(i) a TIMER UNIT for Step B on the host — `sp-cup-observe.timer`/service running `observe-cup-lineups` (all four cups) on a cadence that covers T-3h to T+10 of every stored cup kickoff (one tick, no --loop, every 5 minutes on cup match days, or a calendar derived from the stored fixtures; Code proposes), on the T11 TIMERS list, CI's timers check; until it lands the operator starts the loop by hand on cup days (today's block)."
  - "(ii) The runbook's post-cutover laptop block: `docs/specs/h2-cutover-runbook.md` section 1 step 7 says MLB only; the morning "console" block I wrote today is the operator's shape of it — record it as the laptop's standing routine (backup, MLB, read-only receipts, tally, mirror) so no PL/NFL/NHL/NCAA sync ever runs on the laptop again."
  - "(iii) coverage's laptop view: `cli.py coverage` on the laptop now shows MLB only; the host's coverage file is the one the Cockpit's Today tab should read after the cutover — a one-line note in the Today tab's loader if it prefers laptop/latest."
- **(i), proposed and built:** every five minutes of every day at :00..:55, hours 00-03 and 06-23 UTC.
  - **Why five-minute marks:** a cup kicks off on a five-minute mark, so each T-15, T-5 and T+10 poll falls on a tick. Any other kickoff is asked within five minutes, inside the store's LATE_LIMIT of five minutes.
  - **No H0-3 exemption is needed:** the CI check reads fixed-minute calendars only, and no cup kicks off in 04-05 UTC.
  - **The lock:** a tick with no poll due takes no lock, so the timer never waits on a chain on a day without cup games.
  - **A refusal pages:** a refusal (no DB file, the store not migrated, no key) fails the unit and pages through `sp-notify@cup-observe`, since the store would not be recording.
- **(ii):** the routine is written as the five parts the ruling names. The exact console form is the operator's block of 2026-10-27.
- **(iii):** the Cockpit's "Load latest from host" control already reads `host/latest`. The repo copy's Today note now names `host/latest/coverage.json`. The live Cockpit is the published artifact, so the operator carries the line there.
- **No roadmap move (ARCHITECT 2026-10-27, the EFL schedule finding):** "Step B's first live run is TODAY on the host (two games), not 10-28; the roadmap's EFL line reads 10-27 (today) after all — no move." The 08:30 ET move to 10-28 is withdrawn, and docs/roadmap.json is unchanged.
- **The cups' daily schedule read (#707), the finding verbatim:** "the EFL Cup round-4 dates were a day wrong in the stored schedule for 4 of 8 games (two moved to 10-27, one to 10-29) until a hand sync at 12:16Z; nothing on the host re-reads a cup competition's schedule between the Sunday full-season sync and the 24h window. Fix: a daily cup schedule step (EFL, CL, UEL, FAC) on an existing daily chain (intl-daily or soccer-morning-after; Code proposes), listed in the chain's steps; until it lands, cup days need a hand sync the morning before."
  - **Proposed and built:** `intl-daily` runs every day at 07:20 UTC. `soccer-morning-after` runs Sun/Mon/Tue only, so it would miss the day before a Thursday UEL game.
  - **The steps:** four `sync-matches --competition <EFL|CL|UEL|FAC> --season 2026/27` steps come last, so a failed cup read leaves the intl steps done. One listing read per cup.
  - **Reading for the architect, the season:** the string is 2026/27 for all four, the soccer clubs' form; the window's 10-15 run synced UEL 2026/27. A cup the host does not store is a skipped step (`run sync_competitions first`) rather than a crash.
  - **Not added:** `sync-teams`. `sync-matches` skips a listing whose clubs are not stored (a new FAC round's lower-league clubs), as the Sunday full-season sync does today.
  - **Found on the way, `deploy/hosting/coverage_map.py`:** `scheduled_shadows` credited a chain's shadow export to every competition the chain's steps name. With the cup reads in intl-daily, coverage would have called CL "shadow v2" (intl_elo_v2), which tests/test_coverage_map.py caught. A shadow export now covers the competitions named by the steps before it, the reads that feed it. nhl-daily keeps NHL, and intl-daily names none, as before.

**2026-10-26 — FIXED (#703; ARCHITECT 2026-10-26 17:00 ET: "#703's fixes before the receipt's first run"): the as-of pitcher receipt's live path counts only what it can rebuild. No bar moves.**
- **The findings** (#702's round-2 Codex P2s, verified, carried to #703 under the review stop rule):
  - The P line took a side's path from innings alone, though an ERA the path reads could be incomplete.
  - It took a path from a participant row refreshed after the kickoff, though that row cannot show the pregame identity.
- **The fix** (`scripts/mlb_pitcher_asof_receipt.py`): such sides are counted under their own names, "identity not established pregame" and "not reconstructable", ahead of the path branches. A component's ERA is incomplete when an earned_runs NULL sits in its season sums or, for the bullpen, in a recent window of 10 IP or more, the window the live read blends in. The summary prints the sides whose live path is reconstructed whole.
- **Reading for the architect:** a side with no participant row stays "no pitcher input": that is the live layer's exact path on the stored data.

**2026-10-26 — BUILT (#691, #693): the flip's host.env copy is created 0600 before its bytes (#682's rule); a read error in the cutover's scrub plan is a receipted install refusal. No bar moves.**
- **#691, ruling (ARCHITECT 2026-10-26 12:20 ET), verbatim:** "The flip's shutil.copy2 copy: its own small PR under the same rule, after #673." The rule (on Codex's P1s on #682): "a copy of a file that holds secrets must be created 0600 before any byte is written, and it must live where git can't see it (beside `host.env.pre-cutover-<ts>` under `/etc/sports-predictor/`, root:sp 0640, is the pattern the flip already uses — not in the checkout behind a `.gitignore` line)".

- **#693, ruling (ARCHITECT 2026-10-26 13:00 ET), verbatim:** "#682 round-5 P2: follow-up Issue, not a block (nothing installed on that path; the fix rides with #691)."

- **What it does:** two live MLB rows holding one `mlb_stats_api` id are one game. The command classes each pair from the rows' stored state, keeps one row and retires the other to STALE_ORPHAN with its references re-pointed. Nothing is deleted.
- **Readings for the architect, as built:**
  - **The group:** live MLB rows of every competition (the sync's own lookup since #650), STALE_ORPHAN rows excluded. Three rows on one gamePk are refused.
  - **The class:** 1 = both FINISHED, one score, one kickoff minute; 4 = both FINISHED, one score, two kickoffs; 2 = FINISHED and SCHEDULED; 3 = POSTPONED and another status. Two FINISHED rows with different scores, and any other pair of statuses, are refused as no class of the ruling.
  - **The kept row:** class 1 by (a). Class 2 keeps the FINISHED row whatever either holds, as (c) says. Class 3 keeps the make-up; a POSTPONED row holding references takes (a) ("where one does, (a) applies"), and both holding some is refused. Class 4 keeps the earlier row and takes the later row's date; a later row holding references is refused, because (b)'s keep and (a)'s would disagree.
  - **The provider's current state** (utc_date, status, status_raw, scores, full_time_result) is read from the current row: class 2 the FINISHED row, class 3 the make-up, class 4 the later row, class 1 the kept row itself. No provider call is made.
  - **Re-pointing:** the references, `pitcher_appearances` and `umpire_games` always move; the last two hold one row per source game by their unique indexes. Any other table moves only where the kept row holds none of it. Where both rows hold one (a starter in `match_participants`, `game_weather`, `match_stats`), the retired row keeps its own: counted and printed, never deleted.
  - **The retired row's id:** `mlb_stats_api` moves to `mlb_stats_api_prev`, with `mlb_stats_api_merged_into` and `mlb_stats_api_deduped_at`. The sync's prefetch maps a gamePk to the last row holding it, so a retired row keeping the key could be found and set FINISHED again.
  - **Class 2's predictions** are re-pointed as (c) says. Each carries `factor_breakdown.dedupe_569`, and `evaluate_finished` never grades it ("never graded as calls").
  - **Open for the architect:** the exports pick the latest prediction per match (`export.py`). Where the kept row holds no prediction of its own, a re-pointed class-2 prediction becomes that game's latest prediction, ungraded. The dry run prints each class-2 group's predictions, with how many were computed after the kept row's kickoff.
  - **The training set:** the dry run prints the FINISHED MLB rows per season, before and after. improve's holdout line BEFORE/AFTER comes from the operator's block, which runs improve on two copies of one `.backup` with the live DB untouched.
- **Which database (ARCHITECT 2026-10-27, addendum 169 item 3(c), verbatim):** "its body names WHICH DATABASE it runs on — the twins are MLB rows, and MLB's record is the laptop's, while the host holds the same twins from the pack; my reading is both, laptop first (the MLB record), the host second under its lock, each after its backup; the dry run on each is pasted before the write. The #702 receipt runs on the laptop after the laptop's dedupe (10-28)."
  - **Built for the host run:** the host syncs MLB through the api-sports fallback, which looks a game up by `external_ids["api_baseball"]`. The retired row's `api_baseball` id moves like its gamePk, to `api_baseball_prev`, and the kept row takes it when it holds none.
  - **The fallback's pairing:** `mlb_apisports.sync_matches` pairs our unkeyed rows with provider games first-come, so a retired twin stored first could be linked and set from the provider again. It now never pairs a STALE_ORPHAN row, and a stored key still finds a row, as before. This is Codex's round-2 finding r4382720331, which the host run ruled in.
- **READ AND APPROVED (ARCHITECT 2026-10-27 09:05 ET), verbatim:** "#704 READ: APPROVED (43/43, 0 refused; holdout 0.6601 before and after on 4955→4944; copy B re-plans 0). The laptop apply follows the merge; the host apply rides v1.6.1 tomorrow. #638 closes on the laptop apply's console."

**2026-10-26 — BUILT (lane mlb-pitchers, #507; roadmap step due 2026-10-28; queue order ARCHITECT 2026-10-26 16:10 ET): the as-of pitcher receipt, read-only. The run is the operator's; the declaration (due 10-31) is the architect's. No bar moves.**
- **The step, verbatim** (docs/roadmap.json, lane mlb-pitchers; addendum 63 item 4): "the as-of reconstruction of the pitcher statistics the live model reads, from the stored appearances (docs/historical_backfill_assessment.md tier 1), as a read-only receipt: coverage per season".
- **What the live model reads** (src/walters/training.py, read 2026-10-26):
  - **Starter:** the starter in match_participants, with that pitcher's pitcher_season_stats row for the game's own season (addendum 162 item 1(b)): era, innings_pitched, games_started.
  - **Bullpen:** the team's bullpen_season_stats row (era, innings_pitched, recent_era).
  - Both are season-to-date at their last refresh, so a past game read from them is read with later games in. That is why the backtest needs an as-of rebuild.
- **The receipt:** `scripts/mlb_pitcher_asof_receipt.py` rebuilds those quantities from pitcher_appearances over games that started strictly before each game, and prints per season:
  - games;
  - appearances per side;
  - the model's starter against the boxscore's;
  - the starter as of the game (no stats, opener, or a starter component with its ERA complete or incomplete);
  - the bullpen as of the game (season, and the 10-day recent window at 10 IP);
  - a cross-check against the stored season rows.
  - A NULL earned_runs is counted as incomplete, never filled (law 4).
- **Readings for the architect, as built:**
  - The as-of figures read the model's starter only (match_participants). The boxscore's starter (is_starter) is printed beside it as a comparison and never put in its place, so a side with no listed starter counts as the live layer's missing-input fallback (Codex round 1).
  - The starter identity's provenance is the participant row's source and refreshed_at. The table keeps the last refresh only, so an identity refreshed after the kickoff is counted as such: the pregame identity is not shown.
  - The live path per side follows _resolve_pitcher on the as-of inputs: no pitcher input (no starter listed), the blend, the starter with the league bullpen, the bullpen half-weighted with the starter unknown, or neutral.
  - The recent bullpen window takes the live sync's inclusive lower date, the kickoff's UTC date minus 10 days. The provider's dates are local, so a late game near the bound can differ by a day.
  - The cross-check reads regular-season appearances only, because the stored season row is the provider's regular-season split.
  - A game's season is matches.season as stored.
  - An appearance that joins to no stored game of the season, or to neither team, is left out and counted.
- **The #569 dedupe precedes the run.** Addendum 163 item 4 says "the canonical game ids after the #569 dedupe — the dedupe PR precedes this receipt". The dedupe PR (addendum 153 item 2) is not built yet. Until it lands, the receipt refuses any season in which a statsapi id is held by more than one stored game, naming the match ids. After the dedupe, the STALE_ORPHAN rows are never a game.

- Readings made in this PR. Each is the conservative one (law 4), and each is for the architect:
  - **The results exports** are `<exports>/soccer_PL_results_*.json`, the file name `export-results --sport soccer --competition PL` writes. A file whose `competition_code` is not PL or whose `sport` is not soccer is named and not read. A file that is not JSON is counted as unreadable. The glob does not recurse, so `host/` is never read.
  - **Duplicates.** One row is kept per match_id, from the newest file: by the file's `exported_at`, then by its name. Every dropped copy is printed with both file names.
  - **Graded** means `graded.top_pick_hit` is true or false. Any other value is "ungraded", counted and left out.
  - **The pick and its model p.** The pick is `predicted.top_pick` (`home_win`, `draw` or `away_win`). Its model p is the side's own probability, `predicted.home_win_prob`, `draw_prob` or `away_win_prob`, else `predicted.top_pick_prob` (rounded to 4 places).
  - **The close** is the results row's `graded.close_fair`, read for the same side (HOME, DRAW or AWAY). This is the grading close of `close.graded_block`, which is the book close for a three-way board: `close_from_kalshi` derives no three-way price. A row whose `close_fair` is null, or has no fair for the pick's side, is "no close": named, with `close_stale_book` where the row carries it, and never in the cohort. A `close_reference` of `kalshi_only` or `kalshi` would not be the book close, so it is named and left out. A PL row should never carry one.
  - **The gap** is (model p − close fair) × 100, rounded to 9 places to remove float noise only. A row is in the cohort at gap ≥ `--min-gap-pp`, which defaults to 5 and is printed. Exactly +5.00pp is in and 4.99pp is out. The divergence stored in `graded.model_close_divergence` is not used: the ruling names the gap over the close.
  - **Stale stamps are counted.** `close_book_stamp_age_h` over `close.STALE_BOOK_H` (24) is printed as "stale", with `close_stale_unswitched` where present. The row is never dropped. The close stamp is `close_at`, and its ages are `close_minutes_before_start` (our capture) and `close_book_stamp_age_h` (the quote's own stamp). Whatever the row carries is printed.
  - **Re-dated rows are left out and counted with their label.** A row is void when it carries the export's `redated` label, or when the closing files on disk void it now (`redated.void_label` against the row's `date`). The receipt says which source voided it.
  - **The Desk's final call** uses `exec_cohorts.tally`'s selection, through its `_within` helper. It is the newest closing run's row within `desk_policy.DESK_CLOCK_DRIFT` of the results row's `date`. When no row is within the drift, the newest run's row is used, unless `void_label` voids it. A closing row is that game's only when its `home_team`/`away_team` are the results row's, because match ids are machine-local. Otherwise the receipt prints "no closing row (teams differ)". With no row at all it prints "no closing row". The call is `desk.call`, printed with `desk.pass_kind` on a PASS. A row with no desk block prints "no desk block on the closing row". `desk.pick` is printed only where it differs from the results pick.
  - **The prediction stamp** is the final closing row's `prediction.computed_at`, printed with `prediction.model_version`. Where there is no closing row it prints "not in the closing files". The results export carries no stamp.
  - **Injury inputs** are the final closing row's `input_quality.injuries.{home,away}.count`, the per-side block the guard reads. If that block is absent, `injuries.home_count`/`away_count` are used and labelled as such.
  - **The one-sided guard's state** is `desk_policy.one_sided_injuries` on the row as `desk_policy.normalize` reads it (sport soccer): it fires and names the empty side, or it does not fire. Beside it are the switch in code now (`INJURIES_ONE_SIDED_RULE`) and the Desk's own record at the run (`desk.pass_kind == "injuries_one_sided"`).
  - **The summary** gives graded PL rows, cohort size, cohort hits, and counts (with hits) by the Desk's final call, plus one JSON receipt line. It gives no verdict, no p-value and no threshold judgment.
  - **Read-only.** The script writes nothing and never imports `src.db.database`. A test runs it in a subprocess and checks both.
  - **Addendum 163 item 1, the table.** It is printed for the cohort and for the mirror set. The mirror is the graded rows with gap <= −`--min-gap-pp`, so −5pp by default. Exactly −5.00pp is in and −4.99pp is out, with the same 9-place rounding as the cohort line. Mirror rows need no closing row. They pass the same left-outs as the cohort: void, ungraded, no pick, no close, not the book close.
  - **Hit rate** is hits / n.
  - **The close-implied rate** is the mean of p, where p is each row's close fair for the picked side. Its 95% half-width in pp is 1.96 × sqrt(Σ p(1−p)) / n × 100: the sum of independent Bernoulli variances, as a share of n. The formula is printed on the line.
  - **The model mean** is the mean of the model's p for the picked side, the same p as the gap uses.
  - **The hypothetical return per unit at the close's fair price.** A hit returns 1/p − 1 and a miss −1, with p the close fair. The mean over the rows is printed. The interval is approximate: 1.96 × sd / sqrt(n) of the per-unit returns, sd being the sample standard deviation (n − 1). No interval is printed under 2 rows. The line says "before spread and fee". A row whose close fair is not inside (0, 1) is counted "unpriced" and left out of the return only. The mirror's return comes from the same function, so it is printed and labelled the same way; the ruling reads none for it.

Acceptance cases: 50555 (ALCS Game 7, dropped 10-20) and 50549 (MIL at LAD, dropped 10-16; its own series fields are null, so receipt (2) reads the series' other rows). (c) The coverage map marks a STALE_ORPHAN row as VOID like CANCELLED (closing.py's VOID set already has it); the Today tile stops showing a slate due for it. Tonight's two MLB failure pages are expected and are not a miss; the doctrine receipt for the day notes them as the dead row."
- **Supersedes** docs/ledger/entries/2026-10-17-mlb-if-necessary-rows.md (the limitation accepted on 10-17, addendum 103 item 1: "Nothing dedupes MLB; leave it."). That entry stands as written; the reopening reason is the SLATE stage, which came after it: it reads every non-VOID row of the day as a game, so the dropped 50555 is planned on.
- **Tonight (2026-10-20), the dead row:** the watch's MLB slate at 17:38 ET and closing at 19:33 ET on 50555 (ALCS Game 7, 20:08 ET) are the two expected failure pages, not a miss. They are noted as the dead row in the day's doctrine receipt.
- **Built (a): `python cli.py retire-orphans --competition MLB --season 2026`** (cli.py; the planner src/ingestion/mlb_orphans.py).
  - **Candidates:** the season's SCHEDULED MLB rows with a postseason stage (statsapi gameType F/D/L/W) and no score. Every other SCHEDULED row of the season already past its start (stage R or NULL included) is printed `[not a candidate]` with why.
  - **Receipt (1):** one GET for the whole run: the season's postseason schedule (`{sportId 1, gameType F,D,L,W, season}`, no dates). The params, the answer's game count and dates and every gamePk are printed once, and the verdict per row. ABSENT: the call answered, it lists one game or more, not the row's gamePk, and at least one stored gamePk of the row's own series (its other rows; the count is printed). LISTED: it lists the row's gamePk. NO RECEIPT: the call failed, the answer lists no game, the row has no `mlb_stats_api` id, or the answer lists no game of the row's series.
  - **Receipt (2):** read from the stored rows only (`read_match_series`, the #605 columns' first reader). The series is the rows of the row's season and stage with its two teams either way round, every status. `games_in_series` is the one value its rows carry; needed = (gis + 1) // 2; wins per side over its FINISHED games. DECIDED when a side has `needed` wins over the k FINISHED games and the series ended before this row's game: its own game number after the clinch's (the clinch's stored game number, which must equal k; with none stored the receipt says `after k FINISHED games`), or, with its own number null, the clinch's start before its own (at the same start, NOT DECIDED). NO RECEIPT for: gis null on every row or disagreeing; a gis under 1 or even (a best-of-N is odd: an even N lets both sides reach `needed`, a tie); the columns not migrated; a LIVE game of the series; a FINISHED game without a decided score; two FINISHED rows of one gamePk or one game number; more FINISHED games than gis; a side past `needed`; two FINISHED games sharing the latest start; two FINISHED games on one ET day (one game stored twice under two ids: a postseason series plays one game a day; #631 review); a clinch (the latest FINISHED game) the other side won; a clinch whose stored game number is not k (`a FINISHED game of the series is not stored`, or more FINISHED rows than its number). Two more guards, a FINISHED game or the row with no start, cannot fire on a current-schema DB (`matches.utc_date` is NOT NULL). Each series row is printed with its gamePk, game number, start, status, status_raw and score.
  - **The plan:** retire only on ABSENT and DECIDED. Every other row stays SCHEDULED, labelled `listed`, `not decided`, `no receipt 1` or `no receipt 2`, with both receipts printed. Exit 0 on a completed plan.
  - **The write (`--apply --backup PATH --match-ids ID,ID`):** the apply plans again in its own session (one call) and retires only the named rows whose fresh plan is retire: status STALE_ORPHAN and `external_ids.mlb_stats_api_orphaned_at` (dedupe-matches --orphans' mark). Nothing else on the row changes. A named row planned otherwise is REFUSED and stays; a row planned retire but not named stays. Nothing is CANCELLED or deleted. The state line counts the stale orphans before and after.
  - **Refusals, each exit 2 with no provider call and nothing written, in order:** a competition other than MLB; `SP_SKIP_FAMILIES` naming MLB (the host's api-sports fallback); a `--season` that is not digits; no database file at the configured path (law 5: never created, the migrations' shared guard, #524); `--apply` without `--backup` or `--match-ids` (and `--match-ids` without `--apply`); the backup check; a DB behind the code (`_schema_refusal`, now module level and shared with dedupe-matches). MLB not stored: exit 1, no provider call.
  - **Never inside the watch:** no chain or closing step runs it; a test pins that no CHAINS step and no deploy/hosting file names it. docs/CLI.md's morning Phase 1 gains the dry run, then `--apply --backup PATH --match-ids <the ids the dry run planned>`, after a fresh `.backup`.
  - **Self-heal, no code:** a later sync that lists the gamePk again finds the row by its id (service.py) and sets its status from the listing. The `mlb_stats_api_orphaned_at` marker stays on the row.
- **Built (b):** `_parse_game` (src/adapters/mlb_stats_api.py) reads `codedGameState` before its "S" default and passes it as `status_raw` (a code not given as a non-blank text is None, never "S"). The mapped status and the pre-game score nulling are unchanged. The service stores it on a created row and writes it on an update only when present, so 50555 and 50549, which no sync lists again, keep NULL. No MLB reader gates on status_raw (`retire-orphans` prints it on every series row).
- **(c), no code:** `closing.VOID` holds STALE_ORPHAN (closing.py:144) and coverage marks it void (`"void": st in cl.VOID`, coverage_map.py:243). Tests now pin it: void like CANCELLED, named and not counted, no closing group, the slate due from the day's other game; a day whose only MLB game is retired has no SLATE line, no NO SLATE FILE gap, and `slate` / `slate_line` null; the Today tile shows the void game and no slate; the watch's `due()` forms no group and the slate stage finds no game that day.
- **Readings for the architect (built as stated; each a reading, not a ruling):**
  1. "A window that covers its date ... one call": the season's postseason window, one call for the run (the precedent: `mlb-time-audit`, the whole postseason in one GET). It covers every candidate's date, since candidates are postseason rows only. The strict read's D..D window was not used: an if-necessary game's own day can list zero games (G7's day after a six-game series).
  2. The evidence is the answer's raw gamePks (every `dates[].games[].gamePk`, a null or blank one dropped), not the sync's `held` and not the parsed list. That is more conservative: an entry with no team id or a bad date still counts as LISTED.
  3. Candidates are postseason rows only (F/D/L/W): the arithmetic does not hold for a regular-season series. Every other past SCHEDULED row is printed, so a 50549 stored with a NULL stage shows in the dry run.
  4. 50549's own game number is null: DECIDED when the clinching game's start is before this row's stored start, printed `game number: null (own); read by start`.
  5. "Explicit, dry run first": `--apply` names its rows (`--match-ids`, as merge-teams names its pairs) and re-plans in its own session.
  6. Three guards beyond the ruling's text, each NO RECEIPT (law 4): (a) ABSENT also needs the answer to list a stored gamePk of the row's own series, so an answer that does not cover the series is no evidence about it (both acceptance cases' siblings are listed); (b) a `games_in_series` under 1 or even: needed = ceil(gis/2) decides an odd series only, and an even one can tie; (c) the clinch's stored game number must equal k, the count of FINISHED games (else a FINISHED game of the series is not stored, or one FINISHED row is too many), and the receipt names the game by that number; with none stored it says `after k FINISHED games` (with none stored, k stands in for it, and a FINISHED row storing a number of k or more is no receipt: a FINISHED game of the series is not stored; with no number stored on any FINISHED row, a FINISHED game not stored cannot be seen).
  7. The (b) receipt is taken after merge: one statsapi `sync-matches --competition MLB --season 2026 --date-from <first postseason date> --date-to <today>` on main, after the daily backup. That sync also fills the #605 series fields on the NLCS rows if they were last listed before the 10-18 migration (else 50549 shows NO RECEIPT 2 until it runs). Then the dry run again, then the apply. The PR body's before-merge console is the branch's dry run on the laptop, read-only.

**2026-10-20 — BUILT: the anchored chain, `kalshi-history place-chain` and its read-only `--list` (ARCHITECT 2026-10-20 12:56 ET, addendum 148 item 2, on the design posted on #630). Refs #630, #598.**
- **Ruling (addendum 148 item 2), verbatim:** "#630, the anchored chain — RULED on the twelve questions, one change to the design's center: Q1 after A's ticker clock, M used by A: yes. Q3 STOP: yes. Q4 yes to both (the storage definition of IN STEP; MAX_TICK_DRIFT 2h inclusive plus the time tie). Q5 the fourth note part after the ruling part: yes. Q6 END: yes. Q7 "out of step" only: yes. Q8 N1 and N2: accept both. Q10 yes. Q11 the table only, no exchange call: yes. Q12 the listing mode in the same PR, its console in the body: yes. Q2 and Q9, the change: a shift-capable check IS wanted, because the shifted chain is the case the rule exists for (E17 on 50548 is the ALCS's own example, and every rainout-then-doubleheader pattern is a shift). A member PLACES on the count's game when EITHER check passes, and a result mismatch refuses under both: (a) the clock check as designed: |kickoff − ticker clock| ≤ MAX_TICK_DRIFT and no other unused game within 2h; or (b) the settlement bracket: the row's settled_time is after the count's game's kickoff and before the kickoff of the pair's next game in the list (or no next game within N1's window), the target is FINISHED with a stored winner, and the leg's kalshi_result agrees with that winner. The bracket is the shifted event's own evidence that it settled on that game and no other. A member that passes neither stays held and the chain STOPs (Q3). The dry run prints which check placed each row ("by clock 0.1h" or "by settlement +2.9h, before <next id> <ET>"). Tests gain: E17 placed on 50548 by settlement; a settlement after the next game's kickoff stays held; a result mismatch refuses under (b); a SCHEDULED target never places under (b). Size M, track K2; the PR opens after one of the three slots clears (#631 or #629 merging today)."
- **Built (K-track; `kalshi_settled_markets` is the table the #594 reconciliation reads: money-path):** the design's sections 1-5 with every default the ruling accepted, and Q2/Q9 as ruled: a member places on the count's game when each of its rows passes (a) the clock check or (b) the settlement bracket, a result mismatch refusing under both; a member that passes neither stays held and the chain STOPs. Each row is placed by place-held's own path (its lines, the candles read then, the 2000-character cap), its note `<stored notes>; placed by ruling: <the anchor's ruling>; placed by the chain of <A> [k]: <by clock N.Nh | by settlement +N.Nh, before <next id> <ET>>; <the candles' note>`; one transaction, each row read again as a held row and its side read again. The listing mode reads the table and the stored games only. place-held is unchanged (byte-identical console, rows and refusals over its own test file).
- **Readings, for the architect's read** (numbered; 1-3, 9 and 10 change no behaviour and wait on the architect):
  1. **The dry run makes the candle reads** (the design's section 3 and place-held's own dry-run idiom: the cutoff once, one candle call per row it would place), and never calls the backup check; the listing is the mode with no network call. A dry run with no exchange call at all would depart from the design's section 3 and needs a ruling.
  2. **The settled-after-kickoff receipt** of the design's Q9 is read only inside (b), as the ruling words (b); under (a) a row that settled before its game's kickoff is not held for it (verify's probe: settled 2.1h before 50551's kickoff, still `PLACE HOME by clock 0.0h`). Its settled time and gap are printed on every row.
  3. **(a) on a SCHEDULED target** places (the design's Q9 default: "a SCHEDULED target prints 'winner not stored' and does not fail"); the ruling names FINISHED only under (b). A row with no `kalshi_result` cannot mismatch, so under (a) it places; under (b) it does not (pinned).
  4. **A stored winner** is read from the match's `full_time_result` and its scores (the scores where the result is null, as `vs_close.pair_from_row` reads them); where both are stored and disagree, none is stored (law 4; pinned). A winner is read only for a FINISHED game. A draw (`D`, or level scores) is stored as the outcome DRAW (review fix, Codex P2 on #635): every leg's result is checked against it, so a leg that settled yes on a drawn game is a result mismatch under (a) and (b) alike (before, a draw stored no outcome and (a) skipped the check); see reading 10 for (b).
  5. **"The pair's next game in the list"** is the next game after the count's game in kickoff order, used or not (a used game still bounds the bracket; pinned); "within N1's window": the list runs from the anchor's clock through its date + 11 days (N1's ten and the design's day after), and a member whose game has no next game in it is bracketed by its kickoff alone.
  6. **The pair's games** (CORRECTED; the first build read M's two team ids) are the games the anchor's two names fit one each by `km.fit`, the names read from its stored rows as the matcher reads an event's markets (`kalshi_match._names`), as the design's section 2 says and as place-held fits its match. The ids were the stricter read of which game can be a target but the looser read of the bracket's next game, the time tie and the one-kickoff-minute refusal: a game of the pair stored under a second team row of one club fell out of the list, and a settlement after it placed (verify's probe P6: E17 written on 50548 `by settlement +27.9h, no next game of the pair`). Fitted games of more than one pair of teams, M with them, now refuse the command (exit 2, nothing written), as the matcher refuses PAIR_TIE (`best fit shared by two pairs of teams`); merge-teams first. The fit is `km.fit`'s one-each test across the window, not the day's best fit the matcher takes: a namesake club's game in the window is a fitted game of another pair and refuses the command (`km.fit(("New York Y", "Boston"), ...)` scores the Red Sox against the Yankees and against the Mets 3.5 each, so the matcher itself refuses PAIR_TIE on a day holding both). That is the conservative side (law 4; the events are then ruled by place-held, and the refusal says so: it names merge-teams only when every fitted pair's clubs carry the same two names, since merge-teams pairs only team rows whose names are equal); reading the best fit across the list instead is the architect's. Each member row's side is still read by place-held's own `_ruled_target` on the count's game, so its fit, side and side-held refusals stand (a side another row holds keeps the member held and stops the chain).
  7. **The note's chain part** uses the ruling's example forms, one decimal (`by clock 0.1h`, `by settlement +2.9h, before <next id> <ET>`); with no next game, `by settlement +N.Nh, no next game of the pair through <date>`.
  8. **Out of step** is the identity hold's own read (`identity_holds`), made against the anchor's own markets dated a day on, a probe read for this and never stored.
  9. **A scalar settlement under (a)** (verify F3): a leg settled "scalar" is stored with `kalshi_result` null and `result as read: 'scalar'` in its notes; against a FINISHED target with a stored winner it places under (a) (`PLACE HOME by clock 0.0h`), because the build reads a result mismatch as yes against no only (reading 3). Under (b) it stays held (no result stored for the leg). Whether a settlement that names no winner, on a game that has one, is a mismatch under (a) is the architect's; nothing changed.

Whether the stored draw counts as the bracket's "winner" (it would place a soccer TIE leg settled yes, and both legs of a tie settled no) is the architect's; the build holds.

  - The SLATE line: started-before-it (kickoff after `exported_at` is unstarted; named: the day's games the file has no row for), the day's file (`ny_date(exported_at) == day`; a file exported after the day is neither the day's nor an older one), `older` named (null when a file stands), a file with no row for any game of the day is none, and of the files that count the one holding the most of the day's games stands, then the newest.

- **Readings, for the architect's read:**
  - **"Unstarted at its exported_at" is read by kickoff time** (the stored start after `exported_at`), never by status: the status is now's, and a game finished since was unstarted when an earlier file was written.
  - **"Such a file" (item 5) is the newest file exported BEFORE the ET day that would count but for its export day** (desk calls, every game of the day unstarted at its `exported_at`). A file that could not count either way is not named. It is named first in the brackets of each NO SLATE FILE line, the refused and block lines included (the declared text is the due line's).
  - **Which file stands, of several that count (the review's freshen case):** the one holding the most of the day's games, then the newest. A freshen after the first kickoff writes a file without the started game; the morning file still holds it with its calls, and it stands, so `started before it` never names a game the slate did cover. As built on base the newest stood; this is a reading, and the newest-first rule is a one-line change back.
  - **Item 4 read literally:** a file of the day exported after every kickoff holds "every game of the day UNSTARTED at its exported_at" vacuously, and it counts when it holds at least one game of the day (each game it has no row for is named `started before it`); a file with no row for any game of the day (tomorrow's file, say, exported late tonight) is no slate file of the day, and the gap stands.
  - **Item 8's counts cover every call kind**: PLAY, PASS, LADDER and `no desk call` count the day's rows (by name, as built); `+k` counts the rest. A row of a game of the day called off (POSTPONED, CANCELLED, STALE_ORPHAN: the MLB export keeps a postponed game's row) is a game of the day and no game: in neither the counts nor k. The receipt's `rows` and `calls` are the page's (the day's), and `beyond_day` is k.
  - **The LATE line now prints for any run that starts more than a minute after its due time**: a retry after a failed attempt, a run after a miss or a hold, a deferred slate. A slate deferred or held one tick runs at the next tick, normally a few seconds past one cadence, so it reads `LATE 1 min` (the ruling's words, "more than one cadence"); only a run exactly one cadence after the due time, to the second, is on time. The receipt's `late_minutes` is the whole minutes after the due time either way (`late` says whether the line printed).
  - **The deferral is receipted** (once a day per family, as a hold) so that the LATE line's first tick stays the tick that first found the slate due, and `coverage` shows `held since HH:MM ET (one slate run per tick: …): the slate runs after it`. The next tick is the first after the tick's run ends, so "a minute later" is the run's length plus a minute.
  - **The tick's run goes by kickoff, a retry last** (slate_order): the ruling says "the next family's slate runs on the next tick" and names no order; the fixed order lost slates, so the order is a build choice for the architect's read.
  - **The HELD page exits 3 (NOTIFIED)** like a miss; the receipts table shows it on the hold's key line and does not count it failing (a hold is no attempt). A HELD page whose send could cost the closing its tick waits for a later held tick; if by then the slate is no longer held (the closing ran), no page is owed and none goes out.

  > (a) The closing watch (deploy/hosting/closing.py; the laptop's now, the host's after the cutover) gains a SLATE stage per closing family per ET game day: due at the first kickoff of the day minus 150 minutes, or at the watch's first tick after 06:00 ET when that is later; one run per family per day; it runs the family's prematch steps exactly as the closing run resolves them (sync-matches for the day's ids, odds, injuries/pitchers/lineups as the family has them, Kalshi, predict, then the slate export WITH --desk to the family's slate file in exports/ — nfl_predictions_<date>.json, mlb_MLB_<date>.json, soccer_PL_<start>_to_<end>.json — never the closing's logs/ path), pushes the mirror, and PAGES, card and phone: "SLATE NFL 2026-10-18: 12 rows · PLAY 1 · PASS 11 · exports/nfl_predictions_2026-10-18.json". A failed step pages "SLATE NFL FAILED: <step> — RUN BY HAND: block …" the way a closing failure pages today, attempts 3 like the closing. The closing runs at T-35 are unchanged; the slate is the morning file, the closing is the row that counts, exactly as today's coverage legend says.
  > (b) `coverage` gains a SLATE line per LIVE competition: the newest exports file of that family's slate kind that covers EVERY game of the day by match id, with its exported_at and its PLAY/PASS counts; else "NO SLATE FILE — slate run due HH:MM ET" (or, where the watch is not the machine, "— run block"). Its gap line in capitals: "NFL: 12 GAMES, ROWS 12, NO SLATE FILE". `coverage --json` carries it; the Today tab shows it first.
  > (c) Receipts the watch writes: `kind: "slate"` lines beside the closing lines, with family, date, rows, calls, file, exit; the morning page reads them as it reads the closing lines.
  > (d) Before the cutover the laptop is the machine for every family (its watch runs every minute while it is awake; a laptop asleep at the due time means the first tick after waking — the page says the run was late, with the minutes). After the cutover the host's watch does it for SOCCER and NFL (the fence lifts), and MLB stays the laptop's to the season's last game. The host's fixed-time timers (nfl-predict Sun 14:00Z — AFTER a 9:30 ET London kickoff) are retired by the cutover PR; they are not fixed by hand this week.
  > (e) Test: a synthetic day with one family's games at 09:30 and 13:00 ET: the slate is due at 07:00, runs once, writes the slate file with desk blocks, pages once; the closing groups still run at 08:55 and 12:25; a second tick does not re-run the slate; a failed export pages the RUN BY HAND text and names the block.
- **Ops class, non-gate:** the exports contract and the Desk are unchanged; no model, threshold or call moves. The host's units and timers are untouched (item 2(d): their retirement is the cutover PR's).
- **Built (deploy/hosting/closing.py, the section "slate"):** after its closings, each tick of `closing-watch` runs `slate_watch` per family for the tick's US Eastern day.
  - Due: `slate_due` = the day's first kickoff (the family's stored, non-void games of the ET day, `day_games`) less 150 minutes, or 06:00 ET when that is later. A tick before it does nothing; a day with no game does nothing.
  - One run per family per day, from the receipts (kind `slate`, `slate_state`): a success or three attempts end the day; a refusal or a superseded run is no attempt (380.4, as `_attempts`). Under the lock the receipts are read again (a success or three attempts by then: superseded, nothing run).
  - The lock is the closing's (`acquire_lock`, the chain lock): a slate and a closing never run at once. Held through a 5-minute wait: a miss, the watch keeps trying.
  - The backup: today's, as a closing takes it (`todays_backup` / `take_backup`; a failed backup fails the attempt before any step).
  - The steps: `slate_steps` = `resolve_steps` (the closing's own resolution) for the day's games not started, every step word for word, the export step's included: its `--out` is the closing's own `logs/<run id>.<slate file name>` (addendum 133 item 3(a)); SOCCER's export adds `--start`/`--end` and nothing else. The slate file's names in exports/ (`slate_file`, the family's `export_glob`): `nfl_predictions_<date>.json`, `mlb_MLB_<date>.json` (`--date <date>`, the closing's own), `soccer_PL_<start>_to_<end>.json`. The SOCCER window (`soccer_window`, sp_run.date_vars): a Saturday to Tuesday day takes the round of the Saturday on or before it (10-17 to 10-20 for Sunday 10-18, the file item 4 names); a Wednesday to Friday day takes the midweek override's form, the day to the day + 3.
  - After the steps: the file must be this run's (mtime), carry `desk_meta`, and hold a desk row for every game of the day not started when the steps finished (`missing_from_export` on the day re-read, a game the steps' own sync added to the day included: it fails the attempt, and the next attempt's steps name it; Codex on #600). Then the kept file is linked into `exports/<slate file>` the way the closing writes its closing file (`place_file`: a hard link, then the rename over the name; `slate_file` {file, sha256}; the logs/ copy stays). Then the mirror push (label `slate`). Then ONE page, the card topic (three tries, ten seconds apart) and the screen. Any of them failing is a failed attempt, paged with the RUN BY HAND line. STAGING (addendum 133 item 3(a)): a failure at a step, a check or the link leaves nothing in exports/ and nothing reaches the mirror; an earlier good file of the same name (Saturday's soccer window file, on Sunday) is never replaced by a half-synced one; a page that fails after the push leaves the file standing (it passed) and the attempt failed (the retry re-runs the steps and replaces it again); a push that fails comes after the link, so its checked file stands in exports/ too (as built in the ruled order; open for the architect, below).
  - Late (item 2(d), "a laptop asleep at the due time means the first tick after waking"): judged on the first tick that found the slate due, the earliest `queued_at` of the day's `slate` and `slate_miss` receipts (a hold's, a miss's and a refusal's included; a miss now records its tick and the due time); late when that tick came more than the watch's cadence (60 s) after the due time. A run held for a closing, or delayed by a miss, on a tick that came on time is not late. Its minutes are in the receipt either way.
  - The closings first (item 2(a): "The closing runs at T-35 are unchanged"). One watch process runs one thing at a time, so a slate started shortly before a closing's T-35 kept that closing's tick from starting (a moving-clock repro: the 13:00 closing queued at T-32 and paged at T-27.5 behind a 12:20 MLB slate). A slate now does not start while a closing the watch will still run, for any family of the tick, has its T-35 within `SLATE_GUARD_MIN` = 15 minutes (more than twice the longest any chain has held the lock, seven minutes, addendum 45 P6) or already past with its start more than five minutes off (`closing_ahead`; a family this machine refuses is none); its wait for the lock ends 15 minutes before that T-35. So held, it runs on a later tick, after the closing; each closing it waits for is receipted once (kind `slate`, `held`, that closing: neither an attempt nor a refusal, no page), so the day's newest hold names the closing it waits for now (with only the day's first hold receipted, coverage had named a closing whose run was done on the line above). A lock wait cut short this way is a hold, not a miss. A closing that cannot start holds no slate (`slate_ahead`): while the MLB feed does not answer, an MLB closing is a miss on every tick, never a run (A6), so when an MLB closing would hold a slate the feed's answer is read and, unanswered, the guard reads the other families' closings only (a feed-down MLB closing receipted as a miss had chained the hold through every MLB group of the day: an on-time MNF slate due 17:45 was held to the 20:15 kickoff and missed). An MLB slate checks its own feed before the guard, so a feed that does not answer pages its RUN BY HAND miss at once. But a closing due by the next tick holds a slate first, with no probe, where a probe could not release it or could cost that closing its T-35 (`_hold_unprobed`): a closing with no feed; an MLB closing the tick's feed answer says starts; or, with no answer, a closing with no feed due by the next tick too, or one probe (`FEED_PROBE_MAX_S`, the 8 s timeout plus 2 s) that could reach the first tick that could start that closing (`next_tick`: this machine's first firing after the probe's start at or after the closing's T-35, on its cadence by role, `mirror_role`: the host's timer on every minute's :00; the laptop's launchd firings, a whole number of minutes after the tick's start, since StartInterval keeps its load phase and misses a firing while the watch runs; a firing before the T-35 cannot start the closing, so a probe that costs the watch one costs the closing nothing). Otherwise the slate stage probes once: an MLB closing the feed cannot start holds nothing. The slate stage probes the feed at most once a tick, not at all when the tick's closings did (their answer is the tick's). Both sides cost something before: the probes had cost a closing its T-35 (on a tick whose slates stayed held anyway, the slate's own check and the guard's probe ran after the tick's closings: 49.5 s steps, a 3 s probe, the 14:25 tick ran to 14:30:03 and the MLB 15:05 closing was queued at 14:31:03, T-34.0, where 92c2442 queues it at 14:30:03, T-35.0; a test pins 14:30:03); and the unconditional no-probe hold that fixed it (c789cc1) held a slate, with the feed down, for an MLB closing that could not start, so the slate lost a kickoff cb1261d had caught (Wed 09-23, the laptop waking at 14:12, PL 14:30 and 15:00, MLB 15:05: the SOCCER slate held at 14:25 and run at 14:30 with [522] only, where cb1261d ran it at 14:29 with [521, 522]). The rule above is the verifiers' prototype (proto_c) with the bound of their second (proto_d). proto_c's whole-minute bound alone let a probe cost a closing a tick on the laptop (ticks at :17: a probe from 14:30:14 to 14:30:18 makes launchd miss its 14:30:17 firing and queues the MLB closing at 14:31:21, T-33.7; pinned at 14:30:21, as with no slate stage). The fix for that (f04460b) bounded the hold by the earlier of the next whole minute and the laptop's next firing, and the next review found it held a slate on the laptop where no probe could delay the closing: the laptop's next firing before the closing's T-35 cannot start it, and the laptop never ticks on the whole minute. So a feed-down slate lost a kickoff that cb1261d and proto_c caught (ticks at :52, 38.8 s steps, a 3 s probe: the SOCCER slate held with no probe at 14:29:44.8 by the 14:29:52 firing and again on that tick by the whole minute, then run at 14:30:55 with [522]; cb1261d ran it at 14:29:47 with [521, 522]). The bound is now the first firing that could start the closing on this machine's cadence (pinned: the slate runs at 14:29:47 with [521, 522] and one probe, at 14:29:52 with an 8 s probe; feed up, the MLB closing is queued at 14:30:55, or 14:31:00 with an 8 s probe, as with no slate stage). On whole-minute ticks, where every T-35 falls on a firing, the bound is f04460b's. Pinned on a moving clock: MNF 20:15 with MLB 18:35 to 20:40 and the VPN on from 17:30, the NFL slate runs at 17:45 and the closings and closing misses are the same with the slate stage on or off. The dry run leaves out of the guard the closings its own tick runs first (`after this tick's closings: …`); a closing after them whose T-35 could be inside the guard by the time they end (within the guard plus 15 minutes per planned closing) makes it `would RUN if they end before HH:MM ET, else held: …`, never a plain RUN; with no network, it shows an MLB closing ahead both ways (`held if the MLB feed answers: …; if it does not, …`), and a closing due by the next tick, on a tick with no closing of its own, as a plain hold where it holds with no probe (else both ways); after closings that leave no MLB feed answer (none of them an MLB closing), an MLB closing ahead adds when it holds with no probe (`(held with no probe if they end within 10 s before a tick at or after HH:MM ET)`, that closing's T-35). Pinned on a moving clock (45 s a step): the cross-family case, the late wake at 12:24, a lock held 12:18-12:24, and a wait cut at the guard, each closing queued at T-35 and paged by T-30.
  - Misses (kind `slate_miss`, once per family, day and reason, notified, no attempt): the MLB feed unreachable (A6, as before an MLB closing; the watch keeps trying), the chain lock held through the wait, every game of the day started before a slate ran.
  - Refusals: the closing's own checks (`refusal_checks`). The family refusal (`SP_SKIP_FAMILIES`, MLB on the host) is receipted once per family, day and reason when the watch is run for that family (bare, or with `--family` naming it) and pages nothing; the host's unit runs `--family NFL --family SOCCER`, so no MLB slate receipt is written there, and coverage's `MLB SLATE · NO SLATE FILE — run block block_<MMDD>_mlb_slate.txt` line is the alert. Any other refusal is notified once per family, day and reason (reading 7).
  - The closings: unchanged. Same groups, same steps, same files: a minute-by-minute test day pins them with the slate stage on and off. `notify_failure` gains an optional title (the slate's notices say "<FAMILY> slate"; every closing notice is as before).
- **The paging texts, as built (declared):**
  - Success: `SLATE <FAMILY> <YYYY-MM-DD>: <N> row(s) · PLAY <p> · PASS <q> · exports/<file>` (`1 row` on a one-game day, addendum 133 item 3(c)); a late run adds the line `LATE <m> min: due HH:MM ET, run HH:MM ET`; the machine's line last (addendum 45). Priority default. N, p and q are the written file's rows and desk calls. Another call kind (soccer's LADDER) follows PASS by name (`· LADDER <k>`) and rows with no desk block follow as `· no desk call <n>`, each only when non-zero; neither is folded into PLAY or PASS.
  - Failure: `SLATE <FAMILY> FAILED: <step command> — RUN BY HAND: block_<MMDD>_<family>_slate.txt · attempt k/3`; the third attempt adds `· no further attempt will run today`; the machine's line last (the closing failure notice's shape). The step command is the failing step's line as the receipt records it (`python cli.py …`); after the steps: `export not written (logs/<run id>.<name>)`, `logs/<run id>.<name> carries no desk calls`, `missing from export (logs/<run id>.<name>): match …` (the kept export the run checked, addendum 133 item 3(a)), `exports/<file> not linked (<error class>)`, `mirror push (exit N)`, `page (ntfy did not accept it in 3 tries)`, `backup (…)`.
  - Refusal (not the family's): `SLATE <FAMILY> <date> REFUSED: <why> — RUN BY HAND: block_…`. Misses: `SLATE MLB <date> MISSED: MLB feed unreachable: VPN on, Tailscale off — RUN BY HAND: block_… · the watch keeps trying`; `SLATE <FAMILY> <date> MISSED: the chain lock was held through the 5-minute wait — RUN BY HAND: block_… · the watch keeps trying`; `SLATE <FAMILY> <date> MISSED: every game of the day had started — no slate run`.
- **Receipts (item 2(c)):** kind `slate`: ts/host/release (append_receipt), family, date (ET), run_id, trigger, due, queued_at, ran_at, late_minutes, late, attempt, covers, file, rows, calls, backup, steps (as the closing records them), push, exit; export (the kept export, `logs/<run id>.<name>`; null until the steps resolve), export_written (its sha256) once the file is read, slate_file ({file, sha256}, or {file, error}) once the link is tried (addendum 133 item 3(a)), page once a page is tried, seconds on every attempt but a lock error; failed when it failed, step only when a step command failed, failure_notification. Every attempt's line carries the declared keys (family, date, run_id, trigger, due, queued_at, ran_at, late_minutes, late, attempt, covers, file, rows, calls, backup, steps, push, exit), a lock that cannot be taken included (pinned per path). A hold: kind `slate`, `held`, `closing` {family, start, run_at}, exit 0. A hold, a refusal and a superseded run carry item 2(c)'s keys too (family, date, rows, calls, file, exit; rows, calls and file null). Kind `slate_miss`: family, date, reason, detail, queued_at, due, notified. The closing readers (`closing_state`, `_attempts`, `covered_ids`, `unpaged_called_off`, `last_calls`, coverage's groups) read kind `closing` only: a test pins them beside a slate success and a slate miss. `last_calls` reads the slate file as the morning file (an export no closing run wrote), as it read the prematch file. `sp_receipts` shows both kinds; a slate miss counts as failing.
- **coverage (item 2(b), deploy/hosting/coverage_map.py):** under each LIVE competition's line, `<CODE> SLATE · exports/<file> · exported <ET> · PLAY <p> · PASS <q>` (the newest file of the family's slate kind, by its own exported_at, carrying the Desk's calls and a desk row for every game of the day by match id); else `<CODE> SLATE · NO SLATE FILE — slate run due HH:MM ET`, or `— run block block_<MMDD>_<family>_slate.txt` where this machine refuses the family. The gap: `<CODE>: <n> GAMES, ROWS <r>, NO SLATE FILE`, claimed for a refused family too (it is item 1's alert). A file that cannot be parsed, or has no desk calls, is skipped with its reason on the line, never counted (law 4); a file of the glob with no `predictions` list (a results export, `mlb_MLB_results_<date>.json`, `soccer_PL_results_<date>.json`) is another kind: no candidate, never listed as skipped (addendum 133 item 3(b)); a file whose name dates it more than 8 days before the day, or after the day after, is not read. With no file the line reads the watch's slate receipts (item 2(c): "the morning page reads them as it reads the closing lines"): where the watch runs no slate that day (a success, three attempts, every game started) it names the block, `— run block <block> (<why>: the watch runs it no more)`; else the due time with a failed attempt (`attempt k of 3 failed (<failed>): the watch tries again`), a miss (`missed (<reason>): the watch keeps trying`) or, when the day's newest slate receipt is a hold, the hold (`held since HH:MM ET (<the closing it waits for>): the slate runs after it`) in brackets: the watch receipts each closing a slate waits for once, so the hold names the closing waited for now, `since` the tick that began that wait; and only while that closing is one the watch will still run (`closing.closing_open`, `closing_ahead`'s own test: a hold for a closing done, started, inside T-5 or out of attempts is stale and drops out; on a feed-down day the line had said `held since 21:04 ET (closing MLB 21:40 ET …): the slate runs after it` about a closing that was a feed miss, and, with the writer fix alone, `held since 14:24 ET (closing SOCCER 15:00 …)` at 21:31 about a closing long done). The every-game-started miss counts as done only while no game of the day is still unstarted (the watch decides from the schedule, not from the miss: a game re-dated later into the day is slated on its next tick). `coverage()` carries it as `slate`. exports/ is read, never written.
- **Docs:** docs/CLI.md (the closing-watch row: the slate stage and its pages; the coverage row: the SLATE line and gap), cli.py's help for both, docs/specs/h2-cutover-runbook.md step 5b (what the host's tick now also does).
- **Tests:** tests/test_slate_run.py (the spec's item 2(e) day and its edges; a feed-down MLB closing holds no slate, the MLB slate's own feed before the guard, the guard's one probe, the dry run beside its own tick's closings and beside a second closing 17 minutes after them, a held tick's probe that cost time with the next closing queued at T-35.0, a feed-down MLB closing that no longer holds a slate past a kickoff (the 14:30 game in the slate, one probe) and that tick's dry run, a tick with no closing of its own probing for the MLB closing due next unless a probe could reach the first tick that could start it (a tick at 12:29:00 and one on a :55 phase probe; a slate stage reached at 12:29:55 in the 12:29:00 tick holds), the laptop's :17 phase with a 4 s probe, the laptop's :52 phase (the feed-down slate keeps the 14:30 kickoff with one probe; feed up, the MLB closing queued as with no slate stage), `next_tick` on both cadences, the item 2(c) keys on lines that are no attempt); tests/test_coverage_map.py (the SLATE line both ways, the gap, skips, the refused machine, the hold, the hold over two closings back to back, a hold that drops out once its closing is done, out of attempts, inside T-5 or started, a game re-dated after the every-game-started miss); the closing fixture turns the slate stage off for the closing tests and tests/test_slate_run.py turns it on. The fix round (addendum 133 item 3): a passing attempt links its kept export into exports/ (the same file under both names, slate_file receipted, link → push → page in that order); a failed attempt (an export step that wrote and then failed, a game missing from the file, no desk_meta) leaves exports/ untouched, absent or an earlier good file byte for byte, and pushes nothing; Saturday's soccer window file on Sunday survives a half-synced attempt and is replaced by the passing one; a link that fails is a failed attempt; the steps are resolve_steps' own (SOCCER's window the only insert); the page reads `1 row` / `2 rows`; coverage passes a results export beside the slate file in silence (tests/test_coverage_map.py). After: under the lock, after the superseded check and before the backup and every step, `_export_path_refusal` (the closing's own) refuses it: receipted and notified once per family, day and reason (`SLATE NFL 2026-10-18 REFUSED: the export path logs/<run id>.nfl_predictions_2026-10-18.json already exists (a run of this family entered in the same second, run id <run id>): nothing a run kept is opened for writing a second time — RUN BY HAND: block_1018_nfl_slate.txt`), no attempt, exports/ as the first attempt left it; the next tick (a new run id) retries.
    - `closing-watch --dry-run`: a slate's plan ends with the exports/ file the run links (`then, once its checks pass: logs/RUN.<name> linked into exports/<slate file> · then the mirror push (--label slate) · then the page`). The fix round's own --out change had left the plan naming only logs/RUN.<name>, and SOCCER's exports/ file (the round's window file, `soccer_PL_2026-10-17_to_2026-10-20.json` on Sunday) appeared nowhere in it; addendum 133 item 7 makes this dry run the first slate plan's receipt on the console. Text only.
    - The docs' staging sentence scoped to what the code does: "a failed attempt leaves nothing in exports/" now reads a failure at a step, a check or the link (docs/CLI.md, the runbook's step 5b, closing.py's module docstring and section comment, cli.py's help, the changelog fragment, this entry); the push case is named as built and open (below). The ruling's own words are quoted unchanged.
- **The fourteen open items, RULED (ARCHITECT 2026-10-18 16:10 ET, addendum 133 item 4: "RULED, Code's open items (the numbers are the PR body's)"). Each: what was asked (as the PR body put it), then the ruling verbatim, then where it lands.**
  1. Asked: The feed-down guard's residual trade. With the MLB feed down, a slate may now start inside an MLB closing's guard (that closing cannot start). If the feed answers again while the slate runs, that closing starts on the first tick after the slate ends, late by at most the slate's run (a few minutes: four to ten steps). The alternative is to keep holding while a feed-down closing is ahead, which chains through every MLB group and misses the other families' slates (the finding this fixes). Which way?
     **RULED (verbatim):** 1 — As built. With the feed down an MLB closing is a miss, never a run; a feed that returns during a slate delays that closing by the slate's run at most, and the alternative chains every MLB group and loses the other families' slates (the finding this fixed). The T-35 invariant is for closings that CAN start.
     Lands: as built.
  2. Asked: A bound on a hold, and a page for it. A hold behind closings that can start can still carry a slate past its family's first kickoff, and no page names a hold. Example (moving-clock harness, feed up): a getaway Wednesday, the laptop waking at 14:12; the SOCCER slate is held for the 15:00 closing and then for the MLB closings, and runs at 14:45, after the 14:30 kickoff. Proposed: when a slate is still held with no `SLATE_GUARD_MIN` window left before its family's first kickoff, notify `SLATE <FAMILY> <date> HELD for <closing> — RUN BY HAND: <block>` once. This is a new paging text, so it is not built. coverage's SLATE line now shows the hold.
     **RULED (verbatim):** 2 — The HELD page is APPROVED as declared text, `SLATE <FAMILY> <date> HELD for <closing> — RUN BY HAND: <block>`, once per family and day, when a slate is still held with no SLATE_GUARD_MIN window left before its family's first UNSTARTED kickoff — a FOLLOW-UP PR after #600 (item 5 below), not a hold on it: coverage's SLATE line shows the hold today.
     Lands: the follow-up lane, #602 (one small PR after #600 merges; the declared text above).
  3. Asked: The LATE line's wording. `run HH:MM ET` is the first tick that found the slate due, not when the slate ran. Held, then missed, then run: `LATE 312 min: due 07:00 ET, run 12:12 ET` for a run at 12:41. Proposed: `LATE <m> min: due HH:MM ET, first tick HH:MM ET, run HH:MM ET` (the real run from the receipt's `ran_at`, printed only when it differs from the tick). This is declared paging text, so it is unchanged here (CLI.md says `run` is that tick).
     **RULED (verbatim):** 3 — APPROVED, the follow-up PR: `LATE <m> min: due HH:MM ET, first tick HH:MM ET, run HH:MM ET`, where <m> counts from the due time to the run's start (ran_at) — the operator reads how late the FILE is — and the line prints whenever the run's start is more than one cadence after the due time, whatever held it; `first tick` says whether the laptop slept. The receipt keeps all three times, as built.
     Lands: the follow-up lane, #602 (the declared text above).
  4. Asked: "Covers EVERY game" against a late slate (item 2(b)). A slate that succeeds after a kickoff cannot hold the started game: the export is `--status scheduled`, and the run checks only the games not yet started. So the page says success while coverage shows `NO SLATE FILE` and the gap for the rest of the day. Options: (a) coverage counts a file that holds every game not started at its `exported_at`, and names the started ones; (b) coverage also reads the day's successful slate receipt. Not built: the words are "EVERY game of the day".
     **RULED (verbatim):** 4 — (a), the follow-up PR: the SLATE line counts a file that holds every game of the day UNSTARTED at its exported_at, and names the ones left out on the line (`· started before it: <ids>`); no gap is claimed for a started game (nothing can run for it); the page's own LATE line is the record of the miss.
     Lands: the follow-up lane, #602.
  5. Asked: An older file covering the day. The newest covering file stands as the day's SLATE file whatever its date: Saturday's soccer window file on Sunday, or a Thursday or Saturday NFL file. The gap then stays hidden even after three failed slate attempts that day. Should the SLATE line need a file exported on the day, or read the day's slate receipts? And should the PLAY/PASS counts cover only the day's games? Not built.
     **RULED (verbatim):** 5 — The follow-up PR: the day's SLATE file is a file EXPORTED ON THE ET DAY. An older file never stands as the day's slate, whatever it covers — the operator's rule is a sync on game day, and Saturday's window file on Sunday, or Sunday's NFL file on Monday night, is last sync's. With only such a file the line reads `NO SLATE FILE — slate run due HH:MM ET (newest exports/<file> exported <ET>, not today's)` and the gap is claimed. Until the follow-up lands, the line shows the file's exported_at, which is enough for the operator to see.
     Lands: the follow-up lane, #602 (the declared text above).
  6. Asked: A failed attempt's file and the mirror (money path). The file a failed attempt wrote stays at its exports/ name, as a prematch chain's does, and goes to the mirror (with its latest/ pointer) on the machine's next push. It may have replaced an earlier good file of the same name, such as Saturday's soccer weekend file on Sunday. The alternative: write to a staging path and move the file into exports/ only once the checks pass. Which do you want?
     **RULED (verbatim):** 6 — Staging: item 3(a).
     Lands: built here: staging, item 3(a) (above).
  7. Asked: The SOCCER window. A Saturday to Tuesday day takes soccer-prematch's round window. A Wednesday to Friday day takes the day to the day + 3, the midweek override's form, which is a name soccer-prematch does not write by default. So a Friday PL game gets its own Friday to Monday file, because Friday's prematch window starts on Saturday. Is that the rule?
     **RULED (verbatim):** 7 — Confirmed as built: a Saturday-to-Tuesday day takes the round's window; a Wednesday-to-Friday day takes the day to the day + 3 (a Friday PL game is in no prematch window, so its own Friday-to-Monday file is right).
     Lands: as built.
  8. Asked: What the counts count. LADDER (a staked call) follows PASS by name and is never folded into PLAY or PASS; rows with no desk block show as `no desk call <n>`. N, PLAY and PASS count the whole written file, which can hold more than the day (the soccer window; NFL's 36-hour default).
     **RULED (verbatim):** 8 — The follow-up PR: N, PLAY and PASS count the DAY's games (rows whose match id is a game of the ET day); rows beyond the day follow as `· +<k> beyond the day` when k > 0 (the NFL 36-hour window, the soccer round). LADDER by name and `no desk call <n>` stand as built.
     Lands: the follow-up lane, #602.
  9. Asked: Refused families and the gap. The gap line is claimed for a family this machine refuses (MLB on the host), as item 1's alert. The host never holds the laptop's MLB file in its own exports/, so the MLB gap would show there on every MLB day. Confirm.
     **RULED (verbatim):** 9 — Confirmed: the gap is claimed for a refused family (the host's MLB line names the laptop's block; that is item 1's alert, and it ends with the MLB season).
     Lands: as built.
  10. Asked: Built beyond the spec's words (rule each):
      - the `slate_miss` kind and its three misses;
      - the family refusal receipted but not paged, while other refusals are paged;
      - the third attempt's suffix;
      - the LATE line;
      - the machine line on the slate page;
      - default priority for the success page;
      - the 5-minute lock wait;
      - no slate once every game of the day has started;
      - the 15-minute guard (`SLATE_GUARD_MIN`) and the MLB feed probe it uses.
     **RULED (verbatim):** 10 — Each ratified as built: slate_miss and its three misses; the family refusal receipted and not paged, every other refusal paged; the third-attempt suffix; the LATE line (reworded by item 3 above); the machine line; default priority for the success page (the closing page is the one that counts); the five-minute lock wait; no slate once every game has started; SLATE_GUARD_MIN = 15 and the one feed probe.
     Lands: as built.
  11. Asked: `<N> rows` is literal: a one-game day pages "1 rows".
     **RULED (verbatim):** 11 — Item 3(c).
     Lands: built here: item 3(c) (above).
  12. Asked: A late slate after a closing. A slate that runs after a closing on the same day re-runs predict, which rewrites the stored prediction row of a closed game that has not started. The closing file stays the close.
     **RULED (verbatim):** 12 — ACCEPTED as a known limitation, logged (BACKLOG + Issue, limitation): a slate that runs after a closing of the same day re-runs predict and rewrites the stored row of a closed, unstarted game; the closing file stays the close and the paged call stays the call; a manual re-run does the same today. The fix is a chains change (the predict step scoped to the games no closing has finished with), a later lane, not this PR.
     Lands: a known limitation, logged: Issue #601 (class:limitation) and the limitation line below.
  13. Asked: A game at 00:30 ET counts as that ET day's first kickoff. The day's slate is then due at the 06:00 floor, about 13 hours before a 19:08 first pitch, and the 00:30 game is in no slate.
     **RULED (verbatim):** 13 — As built, a limitation line in the ledger entry (no Issue): no live family has a 00:30 ET start this season.
     Lands: a limitation line below (no Issue).
  14. Asked: The no-probe hold's rule (money path; the verifiers called it the architect's trade: one probe on such ticks against a one-tick slate delay with the feed down). Built: a closing due by the next tick holds a slate with no probe of the slate stage's own when the closing has no feed, or when the tick's feed answer says it starts; with no answer, when a closing with no feed is due by the next tick too, or when one probe (`FEED_PROBE_MAX_S`, 10 s) from the slate stage's start could reach the first tick that could start the closing (`next_tick`: this machine's first firing after then at or after the closing's T-35, on its cadence by `mirror_role`: the host's whole minutes, the laptop's launchd firings). Otherwise the slate stage probes once. That is the verifiers' proto_c with their proto_d's bound, which replaced f04460b's (the earlier of the next whole minute and the laptop's next firing, whatever the machine). Residual: when the tick's closings end within 10 s before a tick that could start an MLB closing, with no feed answer, the slate is held with no probe even with the feed down, and that can cost it a kickoff. The verifiers' jitter has one (feed-down s5, whole-minute ticks): the 14:25 tick's closing ended at 14:29:51; held with no probe, the slate ran at 14:30 with [522], where cb1261d's 8.2 s probe ended at 14:29:59.2 and its slate covered [521, 522]. The built rule leaves s5 as f04460b had it (on whole-minute ticks every T-35 falls on a firing, and the two bounds are one). Measured on the laptop-phase sweep (240 cases: launchd phases 0 to 57 s in 3 s steps, steps of 38.8, 45 and 49.5 s, probes of 3 and 8.2 s, the feed up and down; the MLB 15:05 closing's queue against 92c2442, the SOCCER slate's covers against cb1261d): built, the closing queued later than 92c2442 queues it in 0 cases and the slate loses a game cb1261d covered in 0 (the same as proto_d in 240 of 240); f04460b 0 and 9; proto_c 34 and 3; cb1261d 40 and 0 (every one of those closings later, all with the feed up). On the whole-minute jitter (128 cases: the feed up in 3 s, down in 8.2 s, seeds 1 to 8): closings equal 92c2442's in 128 of 128, to the queued second, no probe under the chain lock, 28,767 probes (92c2442 14,980; cb1261d 39,351); the slates differ from cb1261d's in 5 cases, and the one game lost is 521 in feed-down s5. The alternatives are the unconditional hold (c789cc1: no slate probe ever costs a closing a tick, but with the feed down a slate can lose a kickoff) or the unconditional probe (cb1261d: the slate keeps the kickoff, but a probe can cost the next closing a tick, T-34.0; 40 of the sweep's 240 MLB closings queued later than 92c2442 queues them). Ratify the built rule, or pick one of those. Not tested: on the laptop the bound counts from tick_at, the clock when watch() starts, after Python has loaded, so the real launchd firing is earlier by that load time; FEED_PROBE_MAX_S's 2 s margin is what absorbs it (the harnesses start each tick on its firing).
     **RULED (verbatim):** 14 — RATIFIED as built (proto_c with proto_d's bound). The invariant is the closing's T-35 for a closing that can start; the residual (a slate held one tick with no probe when the tick's closings end within 10 s before a tick that could start an MLB closing, feed down) costs a slate a minute, and a kickoff only in that minute. The two alternatives each cost more: 40 of 240 MLB closings a tick late, or kickoffs lost with the feed down.
     Lands: as built.
