- **Open for the architect (found in the fix round and by its verifiers; built as ruled, nothing changed for them; money path, needs-ruling):**
  1. **A push that fails after the link.** The ruled order is the link, THEN the push, THEN the page. A push that exits non-zero is a failed attempt (`failed: "push"`, exit 1, paged `SLATE <FAMILY> FAILED: mirror push (exit <n>) — RUN BY HAND: …`, the attempt counted), and the file it linked stays in exports/, where it has replaced any earlier file of that name; the mirror copies every top-level exports/*.json, so this machine's next push (the next closing's or slate's) carries it. The ruling names this only for the page ("A page that fails after the push: the file stands (it passed)"); its sentence "A failed attempt leaves nothing in exports/ and nothing reaches the mirror" read whole would cover the push too. Verifier receipt on 3d9adc5: an EARLIER file at exports/nfl_predictions_2026-10-18.json, a push returning exit 1 at 07:00 ET: NOTIFIED, failed `push`, slate_file {file: exports/nfl_predictions_2026-10-18.json, sha256 42ce975d…}; exports/ holds the new file (the same file as logs/20261018T110000Z-nfl-slate.nfl_predictions_2026-10-18.json), EARLIER replaced. Which: (a) the push case as the page case (the file passed; it stands; the next push carries it), the docs saying so; or (b) a failed push restores exports/ (`place_file`'s `kept` hard link can keep the earlier file and put it back, or remove the new name where there was none). Pinned as built in test_a_failed_push_fails_the_attempt_and_pages_no_slate.
  2. **The hard link.** The hard link makes `exports/<slate file>` and the kept `logs/<run id>.<name>` one file under two names. Every export writer opens its `--out` in place (`open(path, "w")`: export-predictions, export-nfl-predictions, export-fixtures), so a later export that writes the same exports/ name (a RUN BY HAND block, a prematch chain such as soccer-prematch's Saturday window file, or a host timer's export before the cutover PR retires it) rewrites the kept logs/ copy as well, and the slate receipt's sha256 then matches neither name. Scratch receipt on the fix: linked, sha256 7f8e5fbbf03b on both names; after one in-place write to the exports/ name the logs/ copy read the new bytes (cadf0b7e745e). The closing's own keep never leaves its two names on one file past the rename. Filling the temporary name with a copy of the kept bytes (the closing's write path for its own document) would keep the logs/ copy as the run wrote it; the ruling says a hard link, so the build is a hard link. Which? The verifiers add two consequences of the link that a copy would also end: logs/ and exports/ on different filesystems make every slate fail at the link (EXDEV: three failed attempts, `exports/<file> not linked (OSError)`, no slate that day) while the closings keep writing their files (not live: on both machines both folders are in one checkout); and a second attempt sharing the run id wrote into the exports/ file through the kept name (closed now by the #442 refusal above, whichever way the link is ruled). The writers that open the exports/ name in place on the same day: export-nfl-predictions (src/walters/nfl_predict.py, `open(path, "w")`; the last step of nfl-predict and of freshen:NFL, which the window service runs on freshen_needed inside T-90, deploy/hosting/chains.py) and export-predictions (cli.py, `open(out_path, "w")`; mlb-preslate, freshen:MLB, and soccer-prematch for the window name).

**2026-10-18 — The laptop's statsapi sync stores each game's own seriesGameNumber, gamesInSeries, seriesDescription and rescheduledFrom on its match row: data only, read by nothing (Refs #476, #478; #605).**
- **Ruling (ARCHITECT 2026-10-18 10:10 ET, addendum 130 item 2(b)), verbatim:** "(b) THE RIGHT KEY IS THE SERIES GAME NUMBER, and it is a 2027 lane, not a patch: #478's lane ("before Opening Day 2027") gains it — KXMLBGAME postseason/series events match by game number: the k-th event of the pair by ticker date ↔ the row whose current seriesGameNumber is k; the date rule stays for the regular season (no numbering). Gate-class, with the ALCS 2026 set (849816/849817/849818 and the three events) as its fixture. DATA NOW, so the 2027 rule has it and so the reconciliation below has a receipt: the laptop's statsapi sync stores `seriesGameNumber`, `gamesInSeries`, `seriesDescription` and `rescheduledFrom` on the match row (additive columns by the unmapped pattern, like #588's; migration by hand after the backup). Code: one small PR, data only, no reader changes its behaviour."
- **The receipt it rests on (addendum 130 item 1(a)), verbatim:** "(a) statsapi (read-only, Phase 2): gamePk 849818 = our 50546, Game 3, Oct 15, Final 2-3. gamePk 849816 = our 50550, played Oct 17 20:08 ET, Final Rays 7-3, now **Game 4 of 7**. gamePk 849817 = our 50548: the Oct 16 game, POSTPONED, rescheduled to Oct 18 21:08Z, now **Game 5 of 7** (rescheduledFrom 2026-10-17T00:00Z). MLB kept the gamePks and renumbered the games by play order."
- **Built (#605), the DATA NOW sentence only:**
  - **Stored.** `matches.series_game_number` (INTEGER), `games_in_series` (INTEGER), `series_description` (VARCHAR(64)) and `rescheduled_from` (VARCHAR(32), ISO-8601 UTC with a Z), all nullable, added by `migrate_match_series_fields.py`.
    - Not mapped in the ORM: the ORDER LINE note of 2026-10-04, as #588 did for `injuries.player_source_id`. Every chain reads `matches`, and the release ritual checks a tag out before its migrations run by hand. A mapped column would fail every one of those queries until the script ran.
    - `sync-matches` writes them after the flush by guarded Core SQL, only when all four exist (`write_match_series`). Before the migration it is a no-op and the sync writes its rows as before.
  - **From each game's own entry.** The statsapi adapter reads the four fields from each /schedule game (`series_fields`) and carries them on `NormalizedMatch.series`. Every other adapter leaves that None, and nothing is written for its rows.
    - A field the entry does not give is NULL, never another game's (law 4). So is one it gives in a shape the adapter does not read: a number given as text or as a decimal, a true/false, an empty or blank text, a time with no zone or with spaces around it.
    - Each field is read as the entry gives it: a number is never read from text (`"5"` is NULL, not 5) and a text is stored as given, never trimmed. An empty or blank description is NULL.
    - A game listed twice in one answer keeps its last entry's fields, the one its status and kickoff were last written from. On the ALCS shape that is the rescheduled entry, Game 5 of 7.
    - A later sync whose entry drops a field writes NULL for it. Rows the sync does not list are untouched.
  - **The api-sports fallback** (the host's MLB path, `mlb_apisports.sync_matches`) never reaches this code: it writes none of the four, on rows it links or creates.
  - **No reader.** No export, Desk, matcher, window card, web page or script reads the columns. The only code that names them is the write path and the migration's receipt (grep on the PR). The test compares the MLB predictions export with the Desk's calls, the results export, the window card and `kalshi_match.place` on the ALCS rows before the migration and after the four fields are stored: identical. tests/test_kalshi_exec_mlb_soccer.py's export test, unedited, passes on a migrated DB where every match row it inserts carries all four.
- **The migration, on each machine (law 5).** Run order: any; the code works before it. The fields only start to fill after the migration and the next statsapi `sync-matches`. Take the daily `.backup` first, then run it by hand:
  - laptop: `python migrate_match_series_fields.py`
  - host: the `--run-migrations` line that `sp_deploy.py` prints for the release that carries it. The host syncs MLB from the api-sports fallback, so its rows stay NULL.
  - It is additive and idempotent: a column already present is left as it is and the rest are added. There is no backfill. Its receipt counts, per competition, the rows carrying each field and the rows carrying none. It refuses with no database file (the shared guard, #524) and with no `matches` table.
- **Receipt (scratch DB, the ALCS payload of the test fed to `sync-matches` through the statsapi adapter):** before the migration the sync updates 50546 / 50548 / 50550 as before (50548 SCHEDULED at 2026-10-18 21:08Z) and logs `series fields stored on 0 row(s) (none: migrate_match_series_fields.py not run)`. After it: 50546 = 3 of 7, 50550 = 4 of 7, 50548 = 5 of 7 with `rescheduled_from` 2026-10-17T00:00:00Z, all "AL Championship Series"; the regular-season row all NULL. The re-run's receipt: `MLB 4 rows · game_no 3 · in_series 3 · descr 3 · resched 1 · none 1`.
- **Not built (beyond the ruling):** the 2027 game-number rule and its gate (#478's lane), the reconciliation read (130 item 2(e)), any backfill of stored rows, any reader. The live matcher is unchanged (127 item 3(a) stands, as 130 item 2(a) rules).
- **For the architect (open questions, nothing built on them):**
  1. A number given as text (`"5"`, `" 7 "`) or a description with spaces around it. This PR reads each field as the entry gives it (the two numbers as JSON integers, the description as text): a quoted number is stored NULL, a description untrimmed. No statsapi payload is kept in the repo, so which shape statsapi sends is not receipted here. Reading a number from digits in text, or trimming the description, is not built. Should either be?

  - "(b) The in-run claims rule reads a STORED row by its stored (match_id, side), never by re-placing it by date.   - "(c) THE BOUND ON "EARLIER-DATED" (Code's first open question): an earlier event of the pair binds only when its ticker date is within 10 days before the event's date. Inside the bound, held rows that the hold never releases are placed by ruling — that is the cost this season; #478's 2027 lane (the series-game-number key, with seriesGameNumber stored from now) retires the manual step."

Held again, or cleared but refused by the matcher, it is left as stored. Nothing with a match_id is written, and a row refused for any other reason is never read again. Before the fix, a held row whose hold cleared was placed by date on the sides a row placed by ruling held (26OCT181708TBCLE on 50548 beside 26OCT172000TBCLE).   - **Out of step on its own date:** the matcher's own rule (addendum 54 item 6), read by `kalshi_match.behind_out_of_step` itself with the clock before every game. Of its two halves only "no game of its two teams on its date" can read there. Its other half, "its date is before the day of the run", is the live list's "still open past its day", which the history path reads as "unsettled". A numbered event is never out of step itself.
  - **Unsettled:** the two settled lists cannot show an unsettled event. A run that lists a clock ticker also lists the series' open markets (`/markets?status=open`, the live sync's own call), for the hold only, never stored. An event between close and settlement (status closed) is in no list read, so it holds nothing under either half (out of step reads only the events the run knows of), and a later event of its pair is placed by date. RULED (addendum 132 item 4(e)): listing the series' closed markets for the hold is its own small follow-up PR.
  - **Earlier-dated events:** every event of the pair the run knows of: both settled lists whole (not only `--since`/`--until`), the stored rows, the open list. The words set no bound in time; addendum 132 item 3(c) sets it: 10 days before the event's date.

  - **"When the hold clears" with the earlier event settled but unplaced:** the words settle it. The hold reads the earlier event's settlement and its own date, never its placement. The ingest never places 26OCT172000TBCLE by date, and the third use of place-held (130 item 2(c)) places it on 50548. - **Ruling (ARCHITECT 2026-10-18 08:15 ET, addendum 122 item 3), verbatim:**

> 3. HOST WEEKLY-FULLSEASON — RULING. Cause is provisioning, not code: `/etc/sports-predictor/fullseason.list` on the host is still the installed example (comment lines only); hosting-h1.md step T9 ("generate the list from the DB, read-only; paste it as the receipt") was never run; the chain refuses by design ("lists no competitions"; sp_run.py fullseason_steps). It has failed every Sunday we hold receipts for — 10-04 on v1.2.2, 10-11 on v1.3.0, 10-18 on v1.4.0 — each time paged, none acted on: the host has NEVER done a full-season resync. I correct my own page: this morning's "host weekly-fullseason 06:00Z resynced the season" line was wrong; nothing ran. Impact today: small — the host is not the writer, the hourly window and the sport chains cover the next 24h, and the laptop's morning block syncs PL and NFL whole-season daily. Impact after the cutover: a law ("full-season weekly") unmet on the writer of record. So:
>
> (a) T9 is a PRE-CUTOVER ITEM, binding: block_1018_t9_host.txt (Tailscale) generates the list from the host DB read-only, prints it, writes every line EXCEPT MLB, prints the file, then runs the chain's dry run (resolved commands only). MLB is excluded by ruling: MLB is a laptop duty to the season's last game; a host api-sports whole-season MLB write beside the laptop's statsapi rows is #569's twin-row shape. The chain's first real run is its own timer, Sun 10-25 06:00Z — the morning page that day carries its receipt, and Friday's cutover ruling is GO only conditional on it (an added condition; the frozen criteria are not loosened).
>
> (b) Code: one Issue (limitation, host) — "weekly-fullseason never provisioned on the host: T9 unrun, failed 10-04/10-11/10-18, paged each time" — closed by the 10-25 receipt; the runbook's preflight checklist gains T9 ("fullseason.list non-empty, dry run printed"); `cutover-readiness` gains a readout line from SP_FULLSEASON_LIST — "fullseason list: N competitions" or "EMPTY → NOT-YET" (one more binding condition on the readout, in the cutover-watch PR or its own small PR); and the fact that three weekly failure pages went unacted is a process finding for the ledger, not a code change: the morning page will carry "failing units" by name from now on (it did today; the first two Sundays predate it).

A missing setting, or a path that does not exist, refuses ("SP_FULLSEASON_LIST missing — refusing to guess the competition list"). Every line that is neither blank nor a `#` comment is one step, `sync-matches --competition <C> --season <S>`, split on the first `|` with both halves stripped. A list with no such line refuses ("lists no competitions").

A Desk call made on a placeholder kickoff is itself a defect; the clock hold is what stops it (ticker clock vs 04:00Z), so in practice those rows are PASS kickoff_clock already. Market-only PASS rows are not calls and are not graded; nothing to void there. Scope stays as #574 states it: the Cockpit, the three ledger ports, the four results exports, the replay inventory. Non-gate (grading bookkeeping, no threshold, no model output), one PR, the 50548 test verbatim."

The re-dated game's fresh closing row is never substituted into the ticket: it is a different call made at a different time. The closing rows are read by match id (`closing_starts`); the Python side never joined by teams or day.
  - Match id (addendum 109 item 2 (a)): the closing rows (the run's export rows) and the window card's rows (`export._fixture_row`) already carry `match_id` and `utc_date`; nothing on them changed. The Cockpit keeps each file row's `match_id` (`normalize`), every call stores it beside its kickoff (`baseCall`; null when the row had none), and the ledger JSON export, which is the stored ledger, carries both. Each result keeps its `match_id` (`outcomesFromDoc`).
  - Pairing (addendum 109 item 2 (b)): a call with a match id pairs with the result row of that id and no other; more than one such row is ambiguous and leaves it open, as the join did. A call whose id is in no loaded row stays open. Paired by id, a kickoff more than 1h from the result's date voids the call, whatever the gap (three days: void). A call without a match id is paired by the ±1-day team join as before and gets `legacy_join` (shown "legacy join": the ledger lists those calls, the void list marks them, the intake note and the P&L block count them). A re-log that reopens a call drops the flag with the label, except on a parlay leg the legacy join already graded (its ticket waiting), which nothing grades again.
  - A match id is machine-local (review of #577): the host and the laptop number matches apart (`deploy/hosting/compare_exports.py` masks it; `docs/specs/ncaa-shadow.md`: "match ids are machine-local and reusable; a mismatch is counted, never graded"), and the Cockpit claims calls from either machine's Desk files ("Load latest from host" auto-claims host rows with host ids). Pairing by the id alone graded a host-claimed NFL call on a laptop MLB row that carried the same number, and voided a call under a false re-dated label when a same-sport row of other teams carried it. The row of the call's id must now also name the call's home and away teams (`normTeam`); a row carrying the id for another game never grades or voids it. The call stays open with `id_mismatch`, listed in the ledger and counted in the intake note (`id mismatch N`), and a later pairing that verifies grades it and clears the flag. The sport is not compared on the id path: the files name it apart for one game (a soccer call, a PL fixtures row; a UNL call, an INTL results row), and a row of another sport naming both teams is that game.
  - Placeholder (addendum 109 item 2 Q2): the code's one definition, `src/ingestion/placeholder.py` `is_placeholder_kickoff` (04:00:00Z, midnight US Eastern), imported by `redated.py` and mirrored in the Cockpit (`isPlaceholderKickoff`, with a parity check in the Playwright script). A recorded kickoff at the placeholder that moved more than 1h reads "void: placeholder kickoff" instead of the re-dated label: one void state (`void_redated` / `redated`), two labels, out of every tally the same way. An unmoved placeholder is graded as before. Every count line now reads `re-dated N · placeholder kickoff M`. The definition carries no sport, so the label follows it for any competition; either label is the same void.
  - Grading: the Cockpit (repo copy; the live one is republished by the architect). A call whose matched result's date is more than 1h from its kickoff gets the label, status `void` and no result, and leaves every tally. A parlay leg void as re-dated is a push (addendum 114 item 1, below). The ledger lists the void calls; the P&L block counts them, and its early-execution count (the n/50 revisit) leaves them out, except a ticket whose every leg moved: a settled push carried by its void legs, counted in the tallies and, executed early, as one early position, as a pushed straight is (the P&L block's Void line, the void list's header and the intake note name that exception).
  - Parlay push (addendum 114 item 1; addendum 115 item 4), the Cockpit's `gradeLedger` ticket loop: a leg void as re-dated, either label, is removed from its ticket (`pushedLeg`): never reopened by a re-log, and, once paired by its match id or once its ticket has settled, never graded at a later intake, so a void the earlier rule could undo at a later intake (a row within the hour of its kickoff) no longer is. A legacy leg (no match id: the ±1-day team join) on an open ticket is checked again at each intake, as a straight is: its void may be the same teams' game of the neighbouring day (#578, LCS-style back to back), not a move, and its own game's row within the hour of its kickoff grades it (the ticket never waits for it: a void leg is out of the remaining legs; review of #577: kept pushed, a three-leg ticket whose games all played on schedule settled on two legs, 1.0u where it paid 2.0u). The ticket is re-priced on its remaining legs the way a pushed or called-off leg already drops out of it (only the winning legs multiply the stake) and settles when every remaining leg has a result, or at once on a losing one (the ticket rule as it was: "all legs win" is then impossible). One remaining leg pays stake / its price, a single's return (`settleReturn`'s). A ticket whose every leg moved settles at once as a push: stake back, net 0, `ticket_result` "push" carried by its void legs, which keep their status and labels; the tallies count it as a push (n, staked, returned; out of the hit rate). The void leg keeps its label, status and units and takes none of the ticket's fields; the remaining legs carry `ticket_legs` (the legs the ticket settled on: 1, a single; 0, every leg moved). A ticket settles once (`ticketSettled`: a leg graded or carrying `ticket_result`). The moved game's fresh row is never substituted: a same-ticket re-log of a leg at a kickoff more than the hour from its recorded one never rewrites it (`movedLeg`), before the void or after it, and a fresh call on the moved game at its new start is its own call, never a leg. A later-day re-log of the ticket (the next day's Desk re-emits it as P-<day2>-<the same signature>; the other legs reprice into the stored ticket by position) keeps the moved leg's fresh row too (`upsertCalls`, `movedFrom`; review of #577: on main and before this fix it was added as a one-leg ticket of its own, 0.25u staked that nobody issued, a second ticket in `settledBets`). Its stored leg: the same game, pick and ticket signature and the same match id, or, a legacy leg, the one on the ticket a sibling leg of the same fresh ticket reprices into. A different match id (the series' next game of the matchup) is never read as moved; a legacy leg cannot tell the two apart and, on an anchored ticket, is kept either way. The ledger's void list says where each void leg's ticket stands (awaiting its other N legs; settled on its other N legs, a single at one; every leg moved, a push).
  - Legacy join, a label (addendum 114 item 2): every call without a match id that a pairing reached (it holds a result, or it is void as re-dated) carries `legacy_join`, whenever it was graded, so the calls graded before the match-id pairing say why they may differ from the rule. Set on every read of the ledger (`labelLegacy` in `loadLedger`), so the ledger views (the list, now folded under its count, the void list's marker, the intake note's `legacy join N`, the P&L block's `Legacy join: N call(s)`) and the ledger JSON export carry it. A label only: status, result and returns are never touched, nothing is re-graded, and a stored flag is never removed by it; an open call with no result is not labelled. An import labels the incoming rows the same way, so an export from before the label is not counted "updated" by it. The Python ports read the flag the export carries; a ledger exported by a Cockpit from before this change carries none on its old graded calls until it is exported again.
  - The ruled test (`scripts/cockpit_redated_verify.py`, 87 checks): legs A, B, C by match id with A 50548 at its old start: A void, units unchanged; the ticket open while C is open; settled as a two-leg ticket priced on B and C when they grade, once; a fresh call on A's game never joins it. A two-leg ticket with one re-dated leg settles as a single; every leg moved, a push (executed early: one early position); calls graded before the change are labelled "legacy join", results and returns unchanged. A later-day re-log of the ruled ticket with A at its new start adds no ticket; a legacy leg voided by the previous day's game of the same teams is graded on its own game and its ticket settles on three legs. No Python port settles a ticket (the ports leave parlay legs out), so the rule has no pytest twin.
  - The results exports (MLB/PL, NFL, INTL) keep the row with its result (the Cockpit grades the fresh call from it) and add `redated`. `nfl-grade` and RESULTS.md leave the game out. Each counts the void rows.
  - The Python ledger ports (`ledger_fills`, `k_receipt`, the value-shadow receipt) leave a `void_redated` call out and count it on its own line, by label. They pair fills to calls by game, side and day, and a fill carries no match id, so that pairing is unchanged; the k-receipt and the value-shadow receipt count legacy-join calls on a line of their own.
  - The replay inventory counts a closing only at the game's own start.
- **Not re-graded (ruled: "nothing is re-graded retroactively"; addendum 114 item 2: "labelled "legacy join" in the exports"):** a call the Cockpit graded before this change keeps its grade and, carrying no match id, is labelled "legacy join". `gradeLedger` never revisits a graded call, and a graded call does not store its result's date. Before this change, the old and the fresh call for one match were both graded on the one result at the new start (the ±1-day join), so such a game counts twice in every tally and still does. 50548 can take this path if the 10-18 results reach the live Cockpit before it is republished with this change.
- **Not changed:** the other readers of `prediction_outcomes` (evaluate, calibration, the web dashboard, `mlb-actionable-receipt`) are untouched; the rulings name grading, the results exports and the replay inventory.
- **Ruled (addendum 114 item 1; addendum 115 item 4):** the parlay question this entry carried (should a ticket stay open while a leg is void as re-dated): no, the leg is a push and the ticket settles on its remaining legs; every leg moved, a push.
- **Open for the architect (#574; the build follows the ruling's words until ruled):**
  1. (needs-ruling, review of #577) The build refuses an id whose row names another game (counted, never graded), the codebase's rule for machine-local ids. Two things it does not decide: (a) a call whose id does not verify, or is in no loaded row while its own game is loaded under the other machine's id (a host-claimed call graded with laptop results), stays open; should it fall back to the ±1-day team join (flagged), or stay open until results from its own machine arrive? (b) a call records no source machine, and a re-log from the other machine's file overwrites its match id (the position key leaves the id out); should a call carry its machine and pair only with results from that machine?
  2. (needs-ruling, addendum 114 item 1) The Cockpit learns that a game moved only from its result row on the new date: a ticket whose leg moved waits for that row (the moved game played) before the leg is voided and the ticket settles on the rest. Settling sooner needs the move from a pre-game row (a later Desk file's row of the same match id at a new utc_date); not built. Is waiting for that row the reading of "a ticket never stays open waiting for a game that moved", or should a pre-game row void the leg?
  3. (needs-ruling, addendum 114 item 1) "settled when they are all graded": the build keeps the ticket rule that a losing remaining leg settles the ticket at once, as a loss, before its other remaining legs are graded (the result cannot change; those legs keep no result of their own). Should a ticket instead wait for every remaining leg?
  4. (needs-ruling, addendum 115 item 4; review of #577, #578) A ticket whose every leg is legacy (no match id) and whose every leg's teams played the day before (both LCS series on back-to-back days) reads every leg void by the ±1-day join at the intake holding the previous day's games, so it settles at once as a push, before any of its games is played; the build before the push graded it on its own games at the next intake. The build follows "a ticket whose every leg moved settles as a push". Should an all-legacy ticket instead stay open (its legs checked again at each intake) until a leg grades or its games' dates pass?

**2026-10-17 — The window page keys QB news by team id and provider player id, the name display only; `injuries` stores the id (#458, #588).**
- **Ruling (ARCHITECT 2026-10-17 10:40 ET, addendum 112 item 10), verbatim:** "#458 — the window page keys QB news by team and player name, so two same-name injured QBs collapse. RULED: key by provider player id, name as display only; the test uses two same-name players."
- **The key (ARCHITECT 2026-10-17 16:55 ET, addendum 117 item 3), verbatim:** "#458 — the key is (team id, provider player id). The ruling named the provider id to replace the name; a player listed on two teams' reports in one window (a trade, a provider error) is two entries, and collapsing them would hide one. Build it that way; the two-team test stays."
- **The limitation (#458, addendum 48 item 4):** the pager keyed each game's QB news by `f"{team_id}|{player}"`. With #456, two same-name entries on one team are two `injuries` rows and two `qb_news` items. If both were quarterbacks, the last item's status overwrote the first's, and a change in the hidden one paged nothing.
- **Built (#588):**
  - **The id, from the feed.** The american-football adapter (NFL, NCAA) already tells entries apart by `response[].player.id` (addendum 47 item 3; the 2026-09-09 raw probe: player = id/name/image). `list_injuries` now returns it as `player_source_id`, a string, None for an entry with none. tests/fixtures holds no injuries payload; the field is the one `injury_entries` and the position lookup already read.
  - **Stored.** `injuries.player_source_id` (VARCHAR(64), nullable), added by `migrate_injury_player_source_id.py`.
    - Not mapped in the ORM: the ORDER LINE note of 2026-10-04, as addendum 35 item 2 ruled for `odds.source_updated_at`. `injuries` is read by every chain: the window card hourly, and `sync-injuries` and the NFL export in the closing chain. The release ritual checks the tag out first and runs migrations by hand afterwards. A mapped column would fail every one of those queries until the script ran.
    - `sync-injuries` writes the id after the flush by guarded Core SQL. It is a no-op before the migration.
  - **The card.** Each `qb_news` item carries `player_id`, null where the row has none.
  - **The page.** A QB is keyed by his team id and his provider id, `id:<team_id>|<id>` (addendum 117 item 3). The name is display only.
    - One id on two teams' reports in one window (a trade, a provider error) is two entries, one per team. Each pages on his own team's games. When one team's game leaves the card, that entry leaves with it, and nothing pages for the other.
    - The `id:` prefix keeps the key apart from the id-less `<team_id>|<name>` key; a team id is a number. Each entry also carries `name_key`, `<team_id>|<name>`. The key change finds a player's id key through it and never parses a key.
    - Before the ruling this branch keyed `id:<id>`. That was never pushed, merged or deployed: no remote ref holds those commits, the host deploys tags only, and the laptop runs `main`. So no window state holds that format, and none is migrated.
- **Rows with no id (law 4).** These are rows stored before the migration and the next sync, or entries the feed lists with no id.
  - They keep the old key, `<team_id>|<name>`, and the page line says `(no provider id)`.
  - Items with no id that share a team and name are one entry holding every status, sorted, and counted: `(no provider id, N entries)`. A change in any of them pages. None is ever overwritten.
  - From one read the ingest keeps at most one id-less entry per name, and none where an entry with an id has that name (addendum 47 item 3, as addendum 48 item 3 rewrote it). So the merged entry occurs only in rows stored before the migration.
- **The first runs after the deploy.**
  - Before the migration, and until the next `sync-injuries` after it, every item has no id, so the keys are the old ones and nothing new pages.
    - One exception: two id-less same-name items on one team. The old state held one entry for them, with the last item's status. Against the entry that now holds both under the same key, that name is a baseline (no delta that run, listed in `qb_rekey.baseline`) only when its status is the new last item's, the exact case the pager before this change was silent on too. So the deploy run is never quieter than that pager. Any other status pages the merged line, and from the next run a change in either one pages.
  - On the first run where a player's id arrives, he is carried from his name key to his id, so a key change is not news. A real status change on that run still pages, by id.
  - Where two or more ids share one old name key (the collapsed pair itself), the players cannot be told apart across the change. If the ids' statuses are the name entry's (the same statuses, sorted; for the old state's one status, that status among theirs), that name makes no delta on that run and is listed in `qb_rekey.baseline`; from the next run each is compared by his own id. Otherwise the ids fold into one name-level line, `Out / Questionable -> Doubtful / Out (2 entries)`, and it pages. The same holds the other way round (ids gone, e.g. a restore from a backup taken before the migration).
  - What a baseline can still hold: a swap of statuses between the two players (which one is Out) on that one run. A change in what the statuses are always pages.
  - The receipt's `qb_rekey.carried` counts the carried players.
- **The migration, on each machine (law 5).** Run order: any; the code works before it. The id only starts to count after the migration and the next `sync-injuries`. Take the daily `.backup` first, then run it by hand:
  - laptop: `python migrate_injury_player_source_id.py`
  - host: the `--run-migrations` line that `sp_deploy.py` prints for the release that carries it (`sudo -u sp sh -c '… deploy/hosting/sp_deploy.py --expect <sha> --run-migrations migrate_injury_player_source_id.py'`).
  - It is additive and idempotent, with no backfill. Its receipt counts, per source, the rows with and without the id. It refuses with no database file (the shared guard, #524) and with no `injuries` table.
- **A rollback across this change.** A pre-#458 pager reads a state this one wrote as its old keys gone and new keys appearing. On the first window run after such a rollback, in one notification (held in quiet hours, 00:00-07:00 ET): each id-keyed QB gives an `off the list` line; each team-and-name key gives one line with the last item's status, so a same-name pair with ids collapses back into one line; and an id-less pair entry gives one `A / B -> B` line. This is not a fix; it is said here so the lines are expected.
- **Not changed:** the window card's T-90 signature. It digests each row's content, so two same-name rows already count separately there; adding the id would change every signature once at deploy and fire freshens with no news. Also unchanged: the QB rule, the closing page and `qb_listed`, which read the rows and see both (addendum 48 item 4). The hockey and soccer injury reads keep no id; their rows stay null and no QB is read from them.

**2026-10-17 — RULED: the window job's MLB Kalshi step's window ends at {tomorrow}+1 day. Read from code, it has since #205; receipt match 41248 (#175, #583).**
- **Ruling (ARCHITECT 2026-10-17 10:40 ET, addendum 112 item 8), verbatim:** "#175 — the window job's MLB Kalshi step (--date-to {tomorrow}) misses games after 00:05 UTC. RULED: the step's window ends at {tomorrow}+1 day; receipt of one late game found by the new window in the PR."
- **Read from code (main 32e0397):**
  - The step: `deploy/hosting/chains.py:251`, `WINDOW_KALSHI["MLB"]` = `sync-kalshi --date-from {today} --date-to {tomorrow}`. sp_run expands `{today}` as the run's UTC date D and `{tomorrow}` as D+1 (`deploy/hosting/sp_run.py:45-52`; D is `utc_now()`'s date, 426-427).
  - `sync-kalshi` (`cli.py:5846-5856`): `--date-from D` is D 00:00Z. `--date-to T` is T 00:00Z + 1 day − 1 µs, the whole UTC day T, since #205 (2026-10-02).

  - The Issue's window (before #205, `--date-to` read as midnight) was [D 00:00Z, D+1 00:00Z]. A first pitch after 00:00Z on D+1 stayed outside it until the 00:05Z run rolled {today}. #205 fixed that (BACKLOG's #204/#175 backfill entry), but no PR closed #175.

A second shows the Issue's case: a 00:30Z first pitch on D+1 is stored by the step from a 23:05Z run on D and refused by the Issue's window.

**2026-10-17 — Every migration refuses when there is no database at the configured path; one shared guard (#524, #579).**
- **Ruling (ARCHITECT 2026-10-17 10:40 ET, addendum 112 item 1), verbatim:** "#524 — migrate_*.py with no DB file at the configured path creates an empty WAL-mode database. RULED: every migration refuses when the file is absent ("no database at <path>; a migration never creates one — law 5"), exit 1, nothing written; one shared guard in the migrations' common helper; a test. This is the 2026-10-06 incident's shape (an empty DB under data/) and it is still open: do it first."
- **Law changed: law 5** ("The database never travels and is never touched casually"). A migration never creates a database: with no file at the configured path it refuses before its first connection. This is the BACKLOG entry #524's "Law changed" section points to.
- **The finding (#524):** the `migrate_*.py` scripts reach the DB through the app's engine (`get_engine()`). Its connect hooks make the missing directory (`do_connect`) and set WAL on a new, empty file (`connect`). The script then refuses ("matches table doesn't exist") and leaves the empty file and its directory behind. Reproduced on origin/main 5e520f9 with migrate_phase7.py: `sports.db`, `-wal` and `-shm` created under a directory that did not exist.
- **Built (#579):**
  - `src/db/migrate_guard.py`, `refuse_missing_db(engine)`. No migrations helper existed (every script imports only `get_engine` from src/db/database.py, the app's engine module), so the guard is a small module of its own.
  - It reads the engine's own URL: the file the SQLite driver would open, `DATABASE_URL` or config's default, a relative path read against the working directory. An in-memory SQLite URL is refused. A non-SQLite URL passes: there is no file, and connecting to a server never creates its database.
  - All 21 top-level `migrate_*.py` call it first in `main()`. migrate_kalshi_settled_markets.py's own #521 check moves onto it, with the ruled words.
  - One test runs every `migrate_*.py`, found by glob, against a missing file in a missing directory: exit 1, the ruled line, nothing created.
- **Elsewhere:** no other migration runs through `get_engine()`. `deploy/hosting/sp_migrate.py` is the host move (`.backup` pack, verify, install over sqlite3), not a schema migration. `sp_deploy.py --run-migrations` runs the top-level scripts, so it gets the guard through them.
- **Not changed:** `database.py`'s `do_connect` mkdir (the app's first run relies on it; out of scope per #524).

**2026-10-17 — kalshi-history asks a 429 again (2 s, then 5 s) and prints "429 retries: N"; the clock-ticker two-rows line names two games (#572).**
- **Ruling (ARCHITECT 2026-10-17 07:20 ET, addendum 104 item 2), verbatim:** "The code treats 429 as retry-next-run (right: kalshi_history.py refuses "for good" only on 4xx other than 408/429), but it has no pacing between candle calls. RULING: Code, small PR, not gate-class — on a 429, wait and retry the same call once (2s, then 5s) before counting it failed; one line in the receipt "429 retries: N". No threshold, no matcher change. Until it lands, the same five commands re-run tomorrow morning as they are (they skip stored markets and ask the failed ones first)."
- **The nit (same item), verbatim:** "for a real doubleheader (two rows hours apart, e.g. 6270 13:05 and 6245 17:35 on 09-25) the line "dedupe-matches has to merge them" is wrong — they are two games; say "two games of the pair that day; the clock does not separate them". Nothing else moves."
- **Built (#572):**
  - A 429 waits 2 s and the same call is asked again. A second 429 waits 5 s and it is asked once more. A third 429 counts the call failed (the next run asks it, as before). "(2s, then 5s)" is read as those two waits; it is one constant, `RETRY_429_WAITS`, if one retry was meant.
  - Each retry is a call against `--max-calls`. A 429 that meets the cap is not asked again.
  - On a clock ticker with no game number, the two-rows line takes the ruled words when its rows are hours apart, the doubleheader case.
  - Rows at one kickoff minute keep the dedupe words: they are one game stored twice (#569), not "two rows hours apart". Where both hold, the line names each.
  - On a date-only ticker the line still names the rows dedupe-matches has to merge. There the two rows are a placeholder and a second row (the NCAA case, `test_two_stored_rows_of_one_pair_on_the_date_refuse_the_event_and_name_the_rows`).
- **Not changed:** the refusal and its reason, the matcher's choices, any threshold.
- **Open for the architect:** the near-twin pairs of #569 (minutes apart, different ids, cause unknown) read as two games under this split. Every dividing line short of the cause read assumes something about them.

  - **A run done (item 1):** a start time of the day with a closing run in the log prints `done (run <run_id>, <exit>)`, the ruling's words.
    - The run id, exit and covers are the receipt's own keys, as `closing.run` writes its receipt line. The runs are `closing._attempts`: a refusal or a superseded run is no run (380.4).
    - Several runs for one start time: the latest success where there is one (`closing.closing_state`: any exit 0), so a later failed run (an operator's re-run of a closed start time; only a watch run is superseded) never hides it; else the latest run, the log being append-only.
    - A done start time is never printed as due. Where the watch still forms a group at it, the done line says what the watch does with it, as the watch decides. Inside T-5, `closing.due` holds it as inside and `closing.watch` records a miss with no attempt: `(inside T-5: no further attempt, the watch records a miss)`. Ahead or due, `closing._under_lock` supersedes a watch run for a start time with a success or three attempts (`closing_state`): `(a successful closing: the watch runs it no more)` or `(3 attempts: …)`. Otherwise `(attempt N of 3: the watch tries again)`. The line then names the group's games the run's covers do not hold (`; not in its covers: …`), a game stored at the start time after the run.

Only the receipt is read, nothing under exports/; no capitals gap is claimed for it (C7's gaps are prediction rows).

Each is ahead, due now (T-35 to T-5) or inside T-5 (a miss: no attempt, no file), by `due()`'s own thresholds. The run time and the file name are closing.py's own (`RUN_LEAD_MIN`, `closing_name`).

**2026-10-14 — RULED (ARCHITECT 2026-10-14 10:01 ET, addendum 67 item 1): the Kalshi settled-market history ingest, `kalshi-history`, writing one new table, `kalshi_settled_markets` (#519).**
- **Ruling (verbatim):** "KALSHI SETTLED-MARKET HISTORY, the ingest (K-track data lane; the Issue of addendum 66 item 6 is its ticket). What it is: a stored record of every settled Kalshi game market in our series, with the last two-sided quote before kickoff, so the backtests and the older-season tests have a Kalshi close where no book close exists. Read-only against the exchange (public endpoints, no key); it writes ONE new table and nothing else — no odds snapshot, no close used by grading, no prediction row is touched; grading keeps reading what it reads today until a later ruling says otherwise. - Command: `python cli.py kalshi-history --series KXMLBGAME [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--until YYYY-MM-DD] [--dry-run] [--max-calls N]`. One series per run. --dry-run lists what would be stored and stores nothing. Default --max-calls 300 (the probe's whole run was 241 calls); the run stops cleanly at the cap and prints where it stopped (the cursor), so the next run resumes; never a retry loop on a non-200. - Sources, both: `/historical/markets?series_ticker=…` (settled before the cutoff; page by cursor) and `/markets?series_ticker=…&status=settled` (settled after it). Candles: `/historical/markets/{ticker}/candlesticks` for the first, `/series/{s}/markets/{t}/candlesticks` for the second, period_interval=1, start_ts = kickoff − 6h, end_ts = close_time. The two candle shapes differ (historical: yes_bid.close / yes_ask.close / volume / open_interest; live: close_dollars / volume_fp / open_interest_fp); read each by its own keys from the kept payloads of 2026-10-14 under logs/ (law 1: enumerate the keys from those files, not from memory); a null price in a zero-volume minute is left null, never filled. - Table `kalshi_settled_markets`: ticker (unique), event_ticker, series, side ('HOME' | 'AWAY' | 'DRAW' | null), match_id (nullable), yes_sub_title, kalshi_result ('yes' | 'no' | null), close_time, settled_time, source ('historical' | 'live'), fetched_at, last_ts (the end_period_ts of the last candle at or before kickoff that carries both a bid and an ask), last_bid, last_ask, last_mid, candles_6h (count), candles_two_sided (count), gaps (minutes missing in the 6h window), raw_first_candle (json), notes. - Matching: the market's event day and the two names go through the shared matcher as the live sync does (src/ingestion/kalshi_match, the same fit, the same pins, the same refusals) against the stored games of that day; a refusal stores the row with match_id null and the refusal reason in notes — refused rows are kept, never guessed, and are listed at the end of the run by reason, like the replay does. - Kickoff for the window: the stored game's kickoff when matched; when unmatched, the ticker's date-and-time when the ticker carries a clock (the MLB shape), else no candles are fetched and notes says so. - Receipts at the end of every run: markets listed / stored / already stored / refused by reason; candle calls made; rows with last_ts null (no two-sided candle before kickoff); the cutoff read at the start. - Tests on the kept payloads (both shapes, the cutoff file, a settled page and a historical page), with a throwaway DB: a stored row's last_bid/last_ask come from the right keys for each shape; a null-price minute stays null; an unmatched market stores match_id null with its reason; the cap stops the run and prints the cursor; --dry-run writes nothing. Gate-class contract fields are not touched, so no backtest is owed; this is an ingest. PR body: the receipt of a --dry-run on KXMLBGAME --since 2026-10-01 is enough (a real pull is the operator's block, after my read)."
- **As built:** src/ingestion/kalshi_history.py, the command, migrate_kalshi_settled_markets.py and tests/test_kalshi_history.py. The table is written and nothing else; nothing reads it as a close until a later ruling.
- **How the matcher is read for a settled market:**
  - These refusals are the matcher's own, unchanged: no pair, no date, no fit, a pair tie, two rows, a date tie, the time gate, no game on the date, a time tie, a side tie, an unknown yes team, two claims (read across events, as one place() call reads it).
  - Four refusals of the live sync are conditions of an open market and cannot hold for a settled one, so they are not read:
    - in play (`now` is set before every game);
    - no price;
    - the spread guard (a settled market's quote is its candles');
    - the run's window (the window here is --since/--until).
  - Each event is placed alone, so "behind an event out of step", a rule between open events, never fires.
- **Law 1, read (addendum 68 items 3 and 5):** the payloads' keys (`kalshi_history.KEYS`) are enumerated from the five kept files of 2026-10-14 11:54Z.
  - Source: the operator's branch laptop/kalshi-payloads-1014 (34723f1), tests/fixtures/kalshi_history/raw/. The raw files never land on main; the branch is deleted after #521 merges.
  - Which key differed: no key of the receipt (addendum 66 item 6) or of the probe's reader differs from the files.
    - The cutoff is `market_settled_ts`, and the lists are `markets` / `cursor`.
    - The market keys are `ticker` / `event_ticker` / `yes_sub_title` / `result` / `close_time`.
    - Historical candles read `yes_bid.close` / `yes_ask.close`, live candles read `yes_bid.close_dollars` / `yes_ask.close_dollars`, and both carry `end_period_ts`.
  - settled_time's key, which the receipt did not name, is `settlement_ts`. It is on all 200 markets of each kept page; the column was null until now.
  - Read in the files besides the keys:
    - A price is a dollar string, and end_period_ts is epoch seconds.
    - A time is ISO with a fraction of 0 to 6 digits.
    - A zero-volume minute of the historical shape carries `price.close` / `open` / `high` / `low` / `mean` null, with `price.previous` set and its bid and ask present (42 of the 292 historical candles; the live reply has none).
    - An empty side of a market's book is sent at size zero (`yes_bid_size_fp` / `yes_ask_size_fp` "0.00" on all 400 markets), priced 0.00 for a bid and 1.00 for an ask (0.00 on the two legs of KXNFLGAME-26JAN25LASEA).
    - A tied NFL game settles both legs as result "scalar" (0.50): 2 of 200 historical, 4 of 200 live. That is stored as kalshi_result null with "result as read: 'scalar'" in notes; the table holds 'yes', 'no' or null.
  - The fixtures are the kept files trimmed: whole objects only, in the kept order and the kept format (tests/fixtures/kalshi_history/README.md names the raw files' sha256 and the rule).
    - The cutoff file is byte for byte.
    - Each page keeps three events (six markets) of its 100 events (200 markets).
    - Each candle reply keeps every candle up to the kickoff the tests store, and the five after it.
- **From the review of the kept-payload commit (an adversarial review, each finding verified by reproduction):**
  - **Two-sided is ruling 9's predicate:** `0 < bid <= ask < 1` (#286, ARCHITECT 2026-10-06, "two-sided = 0 < bid <= ask < 1"; `k_receipt.leg_two_sided`).
    - The files send an empty side at size zero, priced 0.00 (a bid) or 1.00 (an ask). Read as a price, a minute with no bid became the stored quote with a mid of ask/2.
    - In the kept replies such minutes come only after the games end, so no stored value of the kept data changes.
    - This reading of ruling 9 here is for the architect's read on #521.
  - **A fraction of 4 or 5 digits is read whole on Python 3.10** (docs/CLI.md says 3.10+). There, fromisoformat takes only 3 or 6 digits.
    - Without the fix, settled_time was null on 58 of the 400 kept markets.
    - A close_time of 4 or 5 digits (16 of 200 historical) read as missing, and the market was stored with no quote and never asked again.
  - **The --dry-run receipt prints each row's settled_time,** and the run prints how many rows have none.
  - **Tests strengthened where the rewrite on the kept files had weakened them:**
    - the close leaf of each shape on kept minutes whose open / high / low differ;
    - a cap and a failed page or returning cursor in the second list, after the first is read whole;
    - --until's own day;
    - a stored first candle whose price is null;
    - a kept historical page row's result and settled_time;
    - an unreadable timestamp inside the window.
- **Codex P2 on #521 (e988275), fixed: the write gate reads the migration's own marker, not the table.**
  - `KalshiSettledMarket` is mapped, so any `init_db()` (create_all, run by many scheduled commands) creates the table. A run could then write before the backed-up migration ran.
  - migrate_kalshi_settled_markets.py now writes a one-row marker, `kalshi_settled_markets_migration`, by Core SQL. It is unmapped, so create_all never makes it. This is the convention of `ncaa_cfbd.MIGRATION_MARKER` (Codex on #333) and `V2_MIGRATION_MARKER` (#367).
  - A run without --dry-run refuses unless the table AND the marker's row exist. --dry-run still reads without either.
  - **Codex's second P2 (on f0a564f), fixed as the rest of the same fix:** `drop_db()` (`init-db --force`) now drops the marker too.
    - drop_all() drops only mapped tables. A forced reset therefore left the marker beside a recreated empty table, and the gate read "migrated".
    - `drop_db()` already drops the two CFBD markers for this reason (#333), so the convention cited above has two legs. The first push carried only one.

**2026-10-14 — RULED (ARCHITECT 2026-10-14 10:01 ET, addendum 67 item 3, building #487's ruling of 2026-10-13): the Cockpit's fill units are read from the loaded file's own unit basis; FILL_UNIT_CONTRACTS=10 goes.**
- **Ruling (verbatim):** "COCKPIT FILL UNITS (#487; tools/cockpit.html). Ruled on 10-13: the fill's units are the entry cost divided by the unit dollars READ FROM THE FILE's order lines ("1u = $N"), the way desk_policy.file_unit_basis reads it; FILL_UNIT_CONTRACTS=10 goes. The page never hardcodes a dollar figure; a file whose order lines carry no unit basis shows the fill in contracts with the label "contracts (no unit basis in file)", never a guessed unit. Repo copy only, as always: the live Cockpit is republished on the operator's word after my line-by-line read. PR with its fragment; a short note in the file's header comment naming the rule."
- **#487's ruling (2026-10-13, verbatim):** "With the unit declared in dollars, a fill's units are its entry cost in dollars, fees left out, over the dollars of one unit. **2026-10-13 — RULED + BUILT (ARCHITECT 2026-10-13, addendum 60 item 3 and addendum 61 items 4 and 5): a roadmap date moves only with its moved line, checked against the base in CI. PR #503.**
- **#490, ruled in (addendum 60 item 3, verbatim, with one sentence replaced by addendum 61 item 4):** "A pull request that changes docs/roadmap.json is checked against the file on its base. For each lane both sides hold, by its lane id: an earliest_live that differs, and a due that differs on a step both sides hold, needs a moved line on the head. A step is the same step where its what is the same, word for word. The moved line's which is the word earliest_live, or the step's what, word for word; its was is the base's date and its now is the head's. A date set where the base had none needs no moved line. An earliest_live cleared needs its moved line, with now null. A lane or a step that only one side holds needs nothing from this check: the ruling the pull request quotes carries it, and I read it. The check fails the pull request and names the lane and the date. It never rewrites the file."
  - Also: "within a lane no two steps share a what."
  - Where: beside check-fragments, in the job that already reads the base.
- **#492, ruled (addendum 61 item 4, verbatim):** "Setting a first earliest_live is not a move and needs no moved line. Clearing one is a move, and it is how a failed run is written: its moved line has which earliest_live, was the date, now null, and why. In a moved line now may be null where which is earliest_live; was is always a real date. A step's due is never cleared: a step is done, moved, or removed by a quoted ruling."
- **Addendum 61 item 5:** "#494 is in: a milestone with no due_on key is refused, named." And: "One day is singular: 'in 1 day', 'OVERDUE 1 day', '(+1 more step overdue)'. Addendum 59 5(e) named the pattern, not the grammar."
- **As built:**
  - `src/roadmap.py` `check_moves(base, head)` and `check_base(ref)`; run as `python scripts/ledger.py check-roadmap --base origin/<base>`, a step of CI's `fragments` job after check-fragments.
  - It exits 0 when the file is unchanged or every move has its line, and 1 naming each lane and date otherwise (or a head that is not UTF-8, not JSON, or does not validate). It exits 2 when the base cannot be read. It never writes the file.
  - Two readings, each stated in the PR for the architect: "a moved line on the head" is a line the head adds (its moved list less the base's), so a second failed run is written again; and "its base" is the file where the pull request branched (the merge-base, as check-fragments' base...HEAD), so a date main moves later is never charged to a pull request that left the file alone.
  - The adversarial review of the first build (82c1ffe) found six defects, each verified: the base read at the ref's tip, an old line covering a new move, a traceback on a non-UTF-8 file, a line demanded for a due the base never had, a bare --base falling back silently, and tests reading the machine's git config. All are fixed in c6a4682, with tests that fail on 82c1ffe.
  - `validate`: a step's `what` unique within its lane; a moved line's `now` may be null where `which` is `earliest_live` (the key present); `was` stays a real date.
  - `validate_milestones`: a milestone without the `due_on` key is refused, named.
  - The print: "in 1 day", "OVERDUE 1 day", "(+1 more step overdue)".
- Closes #490, #492 and #494.

**2026-10-12 — FINDING + RULED + BUILT (ARCHITECT 2026-10-12 17:38 ET, addendum 54 items 5 and 6; 18:20 ET, addendum 55 items 3 and 4; #476, lane #478): a postponement inside a series puts the next game's Kalshi market on the postponed game's row; on a clock series, an event out of step holds the later events of its two names. PR #477.**
- **Finding (#476), attributed to the architect's read and harness:** Kalshi's rule (`rules_secondary` of KXMLBGAME-26OCT132000CLETB-TB, read through the public API by web fetch at about 5:30pm ET): "If this game is postponed or delayed, the market will remain open and close after the rescheduled game has finished (within two days). If the game is cancelled or rescheduled to over two days away, the market will resolve to a fair price in accordance with the rules." So a postponed game keeps its event, dated the day first scheduled, and the next game of the series keeps its own. On the ALCS shapes (Game 3, 26OCT151800TBCLE, rained out and played Friday 6pm ET; Game 4, 26OCT161800TBCLE, moved to Saturday; the run Friday 11am ET), main and the switch both store the two legs of 26OCT161800TBCLE on Game 3's row. The leg guard stops it only where the later row still holds current legs of the same event. The row shows the next game's prices, and its order line carries the next game's ticker. Not established: whether it has happened on stored legs.
- **Ruling (verbatim, beside addendum 52 item 4, which stands):** "On a series whose ticker carries a clock time, the events of the same two names are read together. An event with no game number is out of step when no game of its two teams is on its date, or when its date is before the day of the run. Dates are read in US Eastern, and a row that is not a game is not one here. No event of the same two names dated after an event out of step is placed in that run, with or without a game number: it is refused under a reason of its own, and its line names the earliest event out of step and says why that one is. Events dated before the earliest one are placed as ruled."
- **As built (src/ingestion/kalshi_match.py):** `behind_out_of_step` reads every event of a clock series before any is placed. It groups events by their two names (case-folded) and reads every market, priced or not. "No game of its two teams on its date" is read on the pair place() would choose (the best fit on the event's day); no fit at all is no game. A market of a later-dated event of the same names that would otherwise take its place on a game is refused under "behind an event of the same two names out of step" (addendum 55 item 3, below). Its line reads `✗ <event>: refused behind <earliest>, out of step: <why>`. The event out of step keeps its own reason (no fit, no game on its date, in play, outside the window). A date-only series is outside the rule.
- **Ruled (addendum 55 item 3, 18:20 ET), verbatim:** "The reason 'behind' and its line are for a market that would otherwise have been placed. A market refused for a reason of its own keeps that reason, and no such line is printed for it." Why: on today's seven open events, on the rows as stored at 4:27pm, the first build refused three later events as behind, with a line each (26OCT161800TBCLE, 26OCT151800TBCLE, 26OCT152000MILLAD). None of them could have been placed, because tomorrow's rows are not stored. Every run of a normal day would print such lines, dozens in a regular season, and the one line that matters would be lost. The architect's sentence of addendum 54 ("it is refused under a reason of its own") let it be built so. As built now: the check sits where a market would take its place on a game, after the window, the side and the in-play test, before the two-claims count. The three shapes of the finding refuse as behind as before, with their lines. No placement moves: the markets it now leaves to their own reasons were refused before as well.
- **LANE (#478, addendum 55 item 4, attributed; nothing built now):** our MLB rows are held one day ahead. So addendum 52's no-game line prints for each pair's next-day event on every run: one or two a day now, fifteen in a regular season. Before Opening Day 2027, either hold the schedule as far as Kalshi lists it, or quiet that line.
- **What it costs (ruled):** the rule only refuses. While Kalshi has not settled yesterday's market of a pair, today's is refused, and the line says so. On the evening of a rainout, the next game's event is refused though its row is right (the receipt's third shape).

**2026-10-12 — RULED + BUILT, FIRST OF TWO PRS (ARCHITECT 2026-10-10, addendum 37 item 2; day rule 2026-10-12, addendum 44 item 1; how the receipt is taken, addendum 50 item 6; finding #413): the Kalshi matcher's module, its tests and a read-only replay. PR #461. The switch of the two sync paths is a PR of its own, called on the replay's console.**
- **Ruling (verbatim):** "A Kalshi market is stored on a game only when its event fits that game: the event's two team names, taken from the event's own markets, fit the game's two teams, one each. One name alone never places a market. Names decide before time: the fit is judged among the stored games of the series' own competition on the event's day, and when the best fit is shared by games of two different pairs of teams the market is refused. The time gate and the run's window then choose only among games of that one pair, and exactly one must pass. A worse-fitting game never takes a market because the best one was outside the window or the gate. Two markets that claim the same side of the same game in one run are both refused. Every refusal is counted by its reason."
- **Day rule (verbatim):** "The event's day is the date in its ticker, read as a US Eastern day. A game is on the event's day when its stored kickoff, read in US Eastern, falls on that date or a day either side. On a series whose ticker carries no clock time that is the whole time gate: occurrence_datetime is an expected expiration, and there it places nothing and refuses nothing. Inside the one pair, a game on the ticker's own date takes the market before a game a day off; where the date cannot separate two games of the pair, the event's markets are refused. Where the ticker carries a clock time, the time gate stays as built, inside the one pair."
- **The receipt (addendum 50 6(b), verbatim):** "The switch is a PR of its own. First, and by itself, main takes the new module, its tests and a read-only replay; the two sync paths stay as they are. The replay fetches each series' open markets once, places them with the new module on the stored games, opened read-only, and stores nothing. For each series it prints what the new module places and what it refuses, by reason, beside the legs main's matcher stored at its last sync, and then every leg that differs: on another game or side, stored by main and refused now, placed now and not stored by main. The operator runs it in the morning block, straight after the day's Kalshi syncs. The switch PR carries that console, and I call it on that."
- **Rows that are not games (addendum 50 6(c), verbatim):** "A row whose status is cancelled, postponed or stale orphan is not a game for the matcher: it takes no market and is not counted among the rows of a pair."
- **The architect's read of the mirror (addendum 50 6(a)):** 930 stored legs of ten series; KXMLBGAME alone carries a clock (38 of 38); 926 legs sit on a game on the ticker's own ET date; the other four are on Florida A&M's game played a day early (two its own, two the Alabama legs main put there). For the time, the day rule drops no leg main placed rightly. Accepted as built (6(d)): a best fit shared by two pairs is refused even where one fits whole and the other by one word of a longer name; the replay's count is read before more is asked.
- **Next:** the operator runs `python cli.py kalshi-replay` in the morning block straight after the Kalshi syncs and sends the console and the kept markets file; the switch PR carries that console. #413 stays open.

  > other, each row as the run's export gave it, and a closing block naming the family, the start time, the run id

  > repeat was not executed: it stays in the ledger as a claim, marked, and it leaves the P&L and the counts that
  > gate sizing. A shadow follows the same rule."

- **Ruling (verbatim):** "sync_odds orders its candidates by kickoff, then id, before the limit is applied, so that the limit means the next N. --match-ids is unchanged."
- **Amendment (ARCHITECT 2026-10-09 19:07 ET, addendum 33 item 2, verbatim):** "The review's finding is real. Your fix keeps my sentence to the letter, and the letter pins a defect: a named list longer than the limit is cut, silently, and the CLI's default limit is 20. The entry's "(no limit)" for the closing runs was not so."
  - "AMENDED: A named game is never dropped by the limit. With --match-ids every named game is priced and --limit does not apply. The order is kickoff, then id, in both modes."
- The change: `IngestionService.sync_odds` (src/ingestion/service.py) orders its candidate query by `Match.utc_date, Match.id` in both modes; `--limit` cuts the list only when no `--match-ids` is given. **Until this PR the limit cut a named list:** `--match-ids` with more games than `--limit` (CLI default 20) priced only the first N in storage order, silently. The `--limit` and `--match-ids` help say so. (The first fix, 8fb84ee, kept the named list as on main, cut included; replaced by this amendment.)
- What it changes: the window service plans `sync-odds --competition C --season S --limit max(n6, 1)` (deploy/hosting/sp_run.py:129-130), n6 being that competition's non-finished games starting before the far-tier edge; that limit now prices the competition's next n6 SCHEDULED games by kickoff, not the first n6 in storage order. The comment in deploy/hosting/chains.py:234-235 ("sync_odds takes the next N scheduled games") is now true. The closing runs price by `--match-ids`: until this PR a closing run naming more than 20 games through `sync-odds` would have had its list cut by the default limit; now every named game is priced.
- Receipt: tests/test_sync_odds_next_n.py, both tests fail on main and pass here: the limit test (`['late', 'mid'] == ['early', 'mid']`) and `test_a_named_game_is_never_dropped_by_the_limit` (`['late', 'mid'] == ['early', 'mid', 'late']`).

**2026-10-09 — FINDING (ARCHITECT addendum 23 item 3 F(1), logged, nothing built; Issue #387; #385): `sync_odds` (soccer) applies `--limit` with no ORDER BY, and the window service relies on it.** The ruling: "F. FINDINGS TO LOG, a BACKLOG entry and an Issue each, nothing built: (1) sync_odds (soccer) applies --limit with no ORDER BY, and the window service relies on it".
- The code: `IngestionService.sync_odds` (src/ingestion/service.py:708-726) builds `select(Match).where(Match.competition_id == comp.id)` plus the season and the SCHEDULED / `utc_date >= now` filters, with no `.order_by(...)`; it collects the rows in the order SQLite returns them and then cuts `candidates = candidates[:limit]` (service.py:725-726). Which N games are priced is therefore the table's storage order, not "the next N".
- Who relies on it: the window service plans `sync-odds --competition C --season S --limit <that competition's window game count>` (deploy/hosting/sp_run.py:129-130, `max(int(n6 or 0), 1)`), on the premise written in deploy/hosting/chains.py:234-235: "sync_odds takes the next N scheduled games". When storage order is not kick-off order (a re-keyed or late-created row, a game moved by a re-sync), the window can price a later game and leave an earlier one in the window unpriced.
- The closing runs do not depend on it: they price by `--match-ids` (no limit). Fix later, its own PR: an ORDER BY `utc_date, id` before the limit (a change to which games the window service prices).

It is read as the newest that any quote in the answer can be; a quote may be older. It is stored and shown as source_updated_at and described in those words, never as the time of a quote. A row without it has an unknown source time, and unknown is never read as fresh."
- **Ruling (verbatim, item 4):** "sync-odds-football stores the source's update time with what it writes: on every odds row, and on every book consensus snapshot it appends. - Stored: `NormalizedOdds.source_updated_at`; the american-football adapter parses `response[].update` to naive UTC (absent / unreadable / no offset = None, never guessed, never our clock). `odds` and `odds_snapshots` gain nullable `source_updated_at` via `migrate_odds_source_updated_at.py` (additive, idempotent, receipt; no backfill: the old rows' source times were never kept). `sync_odds_nfl` writes it on every odds row and on every book consensus snapshot (the oldest of the snapshot's rows; any unknown row makes it unknown, since unknown is never read as fresh).
